ethereum:0x56072c95faa701256059aa122697b133aded9279 — THE STABLECOIN CASH-FLOW BET
⠀
A roughly $1.21 BILLION cryptocurrency.
⠀
A protocol reporting approximately $13.55 MILLION in monthly retained revenue.
⠀
And a token with an existing connection to market buybacks and staking rewards.
⠀
But here's the contradiction.
⠀
Sky generates income from its financial infrastructure.
⠀
It must also offer competitive savings returns, manage collateral risk, and maintain adequate capital.
⠀
The amount available to support SKY depends on what remains after those obligations.
⠀
Is ethereum:0x56072c95faa701256059aa122697b133aded9279 an overlooked investment in established stablecoin infrastructure?
⠀
Or does its apparent valuation understate the risks behind its revenue?
⠀
Let's examine the numbers.
⠀
01 | WHAT IS SKY?
⠀
Sky is the successor ecosystem to MakerDAO.
⠀
Its financial infrastructure supports dollar-denominated assets and associated lending, savings, and capital-allocation systems.
⠀
Three assets require a clear distinction:
⠀
• USDS — the ecosystem's dollar-denominated stablecoin.
• sUSDS — a savings position tied to USDS.
• SKY — the governance token.
⠀
Legacy DAI also remains relevant to the system.
⠀
Buying SKY does not mean holding a dollar-pegged asset.
⠀
It exposes the holder to the market price and economics of the governance token.
⠀
02 | THE NUMBERS THAT MATTER
⠀
November 17, 2026 snapshot:
⠀
SKY Price: ~$0.05159
Market Cap: ~$1.208B
FDV: ~$1.210B
Circulating Supply: ~23.418B SKY
Reported Total Supply: ~23.452B SKY
Reported Maximum Supply: ~23.463B SKY
Circulating / Total Supply: ~99.9%
24H Token Trading Volume: ~$17.3M
SKY All-Time High: ~$0.1009
Decline From SKY ATH: ~48.9%
⠀
PROTOCOL FUNDAMENTALS:
⠀
Tracked TVL: ~$3.94B
30D Fees: ~$27.56M
30D Protocol Revenue: ~$13.55M
30D Reported Holders Revenue: ~$5.49M
⠀
Market figures use CoinGecko.
⠀
Protocol figures use DefiLlama.
⠀
SKY's price history should not be directly substituted for MKR's historical price series.
⠀
03 | THE DIGITAL-DOLLAR OPPORTUNITY
⠀
The ecosystem's opportunity comes from demand for dollar liquidity and financial services.
⠀
Users may want:
⠀
• Savings products.
• Borrowing facilities.
• Trading liquidity.
• On-chain settlement.
• Collateral management.
⠀
USDS adoption can expand the economic base supporting these activities.
⠀
But stablecoin supply is a liability-side measure.
⠀
It is not revenue or profit.
⠀
For context, DefiLlama's latest retrieved USDS snapshot reported approximately $5.36B circulating on November 16.
⠀
That figure is separate from tracked protocol TVL and excludes legacy DAI.
⠀
04 | WHERE THE REVENUE COMES FROM
⠀
Sky's economics include lending-related fees and income from allocated assets.
⠀
The precise mix matters.
⠀
Crypto-backed borrowing responds to market demand.
⠀
Real-world asset income responds to interest rates, credit conditions, and counterparty performance.
⠀
Savings rates influence the cost of retaining stablecoin users.
⠀
The investment question is therefore broader than:
⠀
“How many dollars are in the ecosystem?”
⠀
It is:
⠀
What sustainable margin does the system earn after funding users and supporting its obligations?
⠀
05 | THE VALUE-CAPTURE ADVANTAGE
⠀
Sky's official token guide states that SKY staking rewards are funded through treasury purchases in the open market rather than new reward-token issuance.
⠀
That creates an identifiable connection between protocol resources and token demand.
⠀
This is stronger evidence than a proposal promising that value capture might arrive later.
⠀
However, the benefit still depends on:
⠀
Purchase size.
⠀
Revenue durability.
⠀
Reward distribution.
⠀
Governance policy.
⠀
And the amount recipients subsequently sell.
⠀
A functioning mechanism needs continuing economic support.
⠀
06 | BUYBACKS, REWARDS, AND BURNS
⠀
These are three separate actions.
⠀
A buyback purchases SKY from the market.
⠀
A staking distribution transfers SKY to eligible participants.
⠀
A burn permanently removes tokens.
⠀
Sky's financial dashboard describes part of purchased SKY being earmarked for later monthly burns.
⠀
Earmarking is different from completed on-chain destruction.
⠀
The dashboard's November 16 snapshot reported approximately 46.8 million SKY purchased for 3.07 million USDS over its displayed 30-day window.
⠀
It also reported 30.8 million SKY paid toward staking.
⠀
Those flows should not be described as if every purchased token was burned.
⠀
07 | THE REVENUE MULTIPLE
⠀
Annualizing the latest 30 days of reported protocol revenue produces approximately $165M.
⠀
Against a roughly $1.21B market capitalization, that implies about 7.3 times the annualized revenue run rate.
⠀
That can look attractive.
⠀
But it is not a price-to-earnings ratio.
⠀
DefiLlama's protocol revenue is a defined dashboard measure, not necessarily complete distributable profit.
⠀
Its holders-revenue category also combines buybacks and staking rewards.
⠀
Those figures should not be mechanically added together as independent economic returns.
⠀
The useful measure is sustainable net value reaching the token.
⠀
08 | THE MKR MIGRATION AND SUPPLY QUESTION
⠀
SKY succeeded MKR as the ecosystem's governance token.
⠀
The base upgrade ratio was 24,000 SKY for each MKR.
⠀
Delayed-upgrade penalties can reduce what a migrating holder receives.
⠀
That conversion is different from a conventional venture-capital unlock.
⠀
It exchanges a legacy governance position for its successor.
⠀
Investors should nevertheless monitor:
⠀
• Remaining migration balances.
• Treasury distributions.
• Staking rewards.
• Completed burns.
• Contract and governance parameters.
⠀
No specific upcoming investor cliff is asserted here.
⠀
A nearly fully circulating supply does not eliminate future selling.
⠀
09 | THE BALANCE-SHEET RISK
⠀
Sky's income depends on assets, borrowers, and financial arrangements performing as expected.
⠀
Relevant risks include:
⠀
• Collateral price declines.
• Liquidation execution.
• Credit losses.
• Custody and settlement dependencies.
• Stablecoin confidence.
• Interest-rate changes.
⠀
A fall in asset yields can compress earnings.
⠀
Reducing savings returns may preserve margins while making the product less competitive.
⠀
Maintaining high rewards may protect demand while reducing available surplus.
⠀
These are financial tradeoffs.
⠀
A high historical revenue figure does not remove them.
⠀
10 | THE VALUATION QUESTION
⠀
Using approximately 23.452 billion current total SKY:
⠀
$0.075 SKY implies ~$1.76B valuation.
⠀
$0.10 implies ~$2.35B.
⠀
$0.15 implies ~$3.52B.
⠀
$0.20 implies ~$4.69B.
⠀
$0.50 implies ~$11.73B.
⠀
These are valuation illustrations, not price targets.
⠀
Future burns or other supply changes can affect the calculation.
⠀
The collateral supporting stablecoins is not a reserve that SKY holders can redeem proportionally.
⠀
Therefore, comparing SKY market capitalization with protocol TVL does not establish a discount to net asset value.
⠀
The valuation must rest on governance relevance and sustainable token economics.
⠀
11 | THE BULL AND BEAR CASE
⠀
THE BULL CASE:
⠀
USDS attracts durable demand.
⠀
Lending and asset allocations generate resilient margins.
⠀
Savings products remain competitive.
⠀
Buybacks continue at meaningful scale.
⠀
Staking distributions and burns execute transparently.
⠀
And governance maintains disciplined capital allocation.
⠀
THE BEAR CASE:
⠀
Stablecoin balances contract.
⠀
Asset yields decline.
⠀
Credit or collateral losses consume resources.
⠀
Savings competition compresses margins.
⠀
Token-support spending weakens.
⠀
And investors overvalue a temporary revenue run rate.
⠀
12 | THE FINAL VERDICT
⠀
SKY has a more measurable value-capture structure than governance tokens relying entirely on future promises.
⠀
The investment challenge is whether the underlying financial margin remains durable.
⠀
My assessment:
⠀
SKY is a bet on stablecoin demand, disciplined asset allocation, and sustained revenue-funded token purchases.
⠀
Its strongest argument is an existing economic connection between protocol operations and token demand.
⠀
Its weakest argument is treating current revenue as guaranteed profit available indefinitely.
⠀
The evidence to watch is net margin, savings costs, collateral performance, executed purchases, and actual supply reduction.
⠀
More stablecoins create a larger financial base.
⠀
Productive assets can generate income.
⠀
Competitive savings products consume part of that income.
⠀
Sustainable surplus supports long-term token economics.
⠀
Buybacks make the connection visible.
⠀
Financial discipline determines whether it lasts.
⠀
Bookmark this analysis before the next stablecoin rotation.
⠀
Which has the strongest long-term dollar-infrastructure thesis?
⠀
ethereum:0x56072c95faa701256059aa122697b133aded9279 , ethereum:0x57e114b691db790c35207b2e685d4a43181e6061, or ethereum:0x7fc66500c84a76ad7e9c93437bfc5ac33e2ddae9?
⠀
And can Sky turn stablecoin adoption into sustainable SKY value?
⠀
Drop your view below.
⠀

In-Depth Analysis of the U.S. Stock Market (November 2026): A Critical Turning Point—How Can Investors Seize the Next Wave of Opportunities?
Special Report on the U.S. Stock Market | November 2026 | In-Depth Financial Analysis
I. Market Context: New Opportunities and Challenges for the U.S. Stock Market
The U.S. stock market has long served as a vital barometer for global capital markets. As of November 2026, investors should focus on several key factors: Federal Reserve monetary policy, U.S. economic growth, corporate earnings performance, and the evolution of the artificial intelligence (AI) sector.

The investment logic in the U.S. market has shifted; it is no longer merely about chasing short-term gains. Instead, the focus has moved toward the quality of corporate earnings, cash flow, valuation levels, and long-term growth potential.

For investors, market volatility presents both risks and new opportunities for strategic positioning. The key lies in identifying sectors with sustainable growth capabilities, rather than blindly chasing short-term market fads.
II. Recent Market Performance: Tech Stocks Under Pressure
Based on the closing data from the U.S. stock market on November 16:
- The S&P 500 Index fell by approximately 1.9%, closing at 7,416.59 points.
- The Nasdaq Composite Index dropped by about 2.5%, closing at 24,509.76 points.
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined by roughly 1.4%, closing at 51,608.17 points.
Tech stocks—particularly those linked to artificial intelligence—are facing significant pressure. The market is currently re-evaluating the earnings expectations of tech companies, shifts in corporate leadership, and whether massive capital expenditures will ultimately yield commensurate returns.

III. Four Key Investment Areas to Watch
1. Artificial Intelligence and Semiconductors

While AI remains a major long-term theme in the U.S. capital market, investors must look beyond mere concepts and focus on tangible metrics such as actual revenue, profit margins, and order growth. Companies like NVIDIA, AMD, and other semiconductor-related firms warrant continued monitoring.

2. Cloud Computing and Tech Infrastructure

As enterprises continue to ramp up investments in AI and cloud computing, sectors such as data centers, networking equipment, power supply, and server infrastructure are likely to see long-term growth opportunities. 3. Financials and High-Quality Value Stocks

Amid market volatility and shifting interest rate expectations, companies with stable earnings, robust cash flow, and healthy balance sheets are more likely to attract long-term capital.

4. Healthcare and Consumer Sectors

The healthcare sector offers a degree of defensive characteristics, while the consumer sector serves as a barometer for the actual purchasing power of U.S. households. Investors should focus on analyzing corporate revenue growth, operating costs, and shifts in consumer demand.
IV. Key Risks Facing the U.S. Stock Market in Late 2026
Three areas currently warrant particular attention:
- Interest Rate Risk: If inflation remains persistently above target levels, the Federal Reserve may maintain a tighter monetary policy, thereby increasing corporate financing costs.
- Valuation Risk: Should the earnings growth of technology companies fall short of market expectations, stocks with high valuations could face further downward adjustments.
- Economic Risk: Fluctuations in consumer purchasing power, the labor market, and corporate capital expenditures could all impact the U.S. economy and the performance of publicly traded companies.
U.S. Bank’s economic outlook for November 2026 notes that inflation remains "sticky" and anticipates that the Federal Reserve may implement further interest rate hikes in December. Consequently, investors should carefully evaluate how changes in interest rates might affect stock valuations.
U.S. Bank+1

V. Investment Strategy: Shifting from Short-Term Speculation to Long-Term Value
Given the current market environment, investors may wish to adopt a more rational investment approach.

First, avoid concentrating capital in a single "hot" stock; instead, diversify across sectors and asset classes. Second, pay close attention to corporate financial reports—specifically revenue growth, net profit, free cash flow, and forward-looking guidance.

Long-term investors might consider a phased entry strategy, avoiding the deployment of all capital at once when market sentiment is at its peak. Short-term traders, meanwhile, should place greater emphasis on trading volume, price trends, support levels, and disciplined use of stop-loss orders.
VI. Future Market Outlook
For the remainder of 2026, the U.S. stock market is likely to remain driven by developments in the artificial intelligence sector, inflation data, Federal Reserve policy, and corporate earnings reports.

Of particular note is the upcoming earnings release from NVIDIA. This is not only relevant to market sentiment within the semiconductor industry, but also serves as a key indicator for gauging the intensity of investment in the AI ​​sector.
Reuters+1

If corporate earnings continue to grow, the market may regain momentum; conversely, if earnings fall short of expectations—compounded by the pressure of rising interest rates—the market could face a more pronounced valuation adjustment.
VII. Summary and Conclusion
The U.S. stock market is currently in a phase characterized by both opportunities and risks. Sectors such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors, cloud computing, and healthcare continue to offer long-term investment value worth exploring, though short-term market volatility cannot be overlooked.

Truly successful investing is not about predicting every market fluctuation; rather, it involves identifying companies with long-term competitive advantages through thorough research, sound valuation, and rigorous risk management—even within an uncertain market environment.

Investors should remain patient—avoiding both the impulse to chase market highs and the tendency to panic-sell—while grounding their decisions in fundamentals and prioritizing risk management.

I am on the buy-side of regulated AI. 

I agree that distribution is the moat for $TAO. But I'd argue the biggest distribution opportunity isn't consumer AI. It's enterprise AI.

With roughly $400B in annual enterprise AI spending, even a small share could transform Bittensor's economics.

Six months ago, I proposed the four bridges Bittensor needs to cross to capture that opportunity. Here's my progress report, grading each on whether we're becoming a place where enterprises want to invest their capital and entrust their most valuable AI work.

1. Attract breakthrough AI intellectual property — Mixed progress.

Can Bittensor become the preferred destination for innovators with valuable AI technology, rather than another startup or a licensing deal with Big Tech?

We're attracting more builders and generating real subnet revenue. Encouraging, but the bigger test is whether truly differentiated enterprise-grade IP increasingly chooses Bittensor first. That remains unproven.

2. Make decentralized AI preferable to centralized AI — Significant progress.

Why would an enterprise trust thousands of unknown miners instead of one established provider?

The answer may be that it doesn't have to trust either. Mathematical privacy could allow decentralized machines to perform AI computations without ever seeing the customer's confidential information.

That's a remarkable inversion: decentralization goes from introducing a trust problem to potentially eliminating it.

3. Make Bittensor transparent, verifiable and audit-ready — Still the biggest gap.

Can investors independently verify subnet economics? Can enterprise buyers prove which model ran, what computation occurred, and whether the result was correct?

Today, too much still depends on estimates and assertions. Enterprises need auditable evidence, not promises.

Cryptographic proofs and end-to-end evidence chains could change that, making both the work and the economics independently verifiable.

4. Make Bittensor safe for truly sensitive enterprise work — The opportunity is becoming clearer.

Can a company safely use AI for its most confidential legal, financial, strategic or proprietary information?

Today, centralized AI generally requires trusting another company with that information. Math-private AI offers something fundamentally different: a compute provider that cannot disclose secrets it never possessed.

For sensitive workloads, that could become an extraordinary competitive advantage.

The bottom line: The prize isn't simply more emissions or a bigger crypto-native economy. It's enterprise investment and a share of the hundreds of billions already being spent on AI.

Just 0.1% of a $400B market is $400M annually. One percent is $4B.

There's meaningful progress on all four bridges, but none is finished. The question is whether Bittensor can turn its technical promise into something enterprises will fund, buy and trust.

Six months later, I'm still taking the bet.

text:
School Assignment Bearing Ja'Niyah’s Name Found in Gary Abandoned House — Never Turned Over to FBI or Police

Missing Lost And Trafficked 
Lured Lost And Unsolved

GARY, Ind. — A school assignment bearing the handwritten name “Ja’Niyah” was recovered from an abandoned house in the 2500 block of Connecticut Street and never submitted to the FBI or Gary Police Department, according to recent updates from the social media news platform, Missing Lost And Trafficked.

The document was reportedly retrieved by Lorenzo Longoria, founder of Team NWI Independent Search Team, a volunteer search-and-rescue organization based in Northwest Indiana, during efforts related to another missing person case.

 An eye witness source, who requested anonymity told Missing Lost And Trafficked that Longoria did not turn the assignment over to federal or local investigators. 

 Amanda Agr discussed the retrieval on the Nov. 12, 2026, episode of the podcast “The Missing Struggle,” hosted on Team Canine of NWI’s YouTube channel.

The abandoned property, located near East 25th Avenue, was described as a house frequented by squatters. 

Emma Baum was reportedly dropped off at
 the same location on Oct. 10, 2024. The assignment’s presence there has drawn attention because of its potential to place physical material connected to Ja’Niyah McMichael at a site tied to other activity under scrutiny in the broader search for missing people in Gary.

Ja’Niyah McMichael, then 13, was reported missing by her mother, Jasmine McMichael, on Aug. 12, 2024, from the 1900 block of Malcolm X Boulevard (also referred to as Virginia Street). 

She was last seen the evening before she was due to start eighth grade, wearing black pajama pants, a black hoodie and black-and-red shoes. 

The FBI and Gary Police Department have said they believe she may be the victim of foul play. A combined reward of at least $20,000 has been offered for information leading to an arrest and conviction.

Missing Lost And Trafficked has framed the assignment discovery against a series of allegations circulating in the case. In private Facebook Messenger messages, Jeffrey Farmer, a registered sex offender, claimed Ja’Niyah was sold by her mother to Antwon Butler to settle a drug debt, was abused and was killed.

 Farmer alleged she was thrown into the Grand Calumet River in August 2024 near Broadway Street, where the river intersects the northern end of downtown Gary near the main entrance to the U.S. Steel Gary Works facility at 1 North Broadway.

 MLAT  has also pointed to geographic connections. Kevin Kizer resided in the 1900 block of Carolina Street on Aug. 12, 2024 — the day Ja’Niyah was reported missing — a location described as directly behind or a short walk from the 1900 block of Virginia Street/Malcolm X Boulevard where she was last seen. Kizer has a documented criminal history that includes aggravated battery, kidnapping with moderate bodily injury, confinement with moderate bodily injury, domestic battery involving a pregnant woman, strangulation and intimidation.

 Separately, Marietta Banks, also known as “Pebbles,” told the group that Kizer assisted Butler in removing a deceased Emma Baum from her apartment on Oct. 10, 2024.

Additional context cited by Missing Lost And Trafficked includes an incident on Sept. 16, 2024, in which Dalia Guerrero, Ja’Niyah’s maternal grandmother, sought police assistance after being threatened by family members of Ja’Niyah’s mother’s girlfriend while near the Grand Calumet River in the 2800 block of Georgia Street.

MLAT  has repeatedly urged a specialized underwater search of the Grand Calumet River. Ohio Special Response Team offered its resources for that effort. Gary Police Chief Derrick Cannon rejected the offer amid the accusations leveled by Jeffrey Farmer.

The school assignment’s recovery and the decision not to submit it to authorities have intensified questions about how volunteer-found potential evidence is handled in a case that has already stretched more than two years.

 Investigators continue to treat the disappearance as an active investigation involving possible foul play.
Anyone with information about Ja’Niyah McMichael’s disappearance is urged to contact the FBI at 1-800-CALL-FBI (1-800-225-5324) or submit a tip online at https://t.co/o9SNTsfpIN. Tips may also be provided to the Gary Police Department.

text:
🇯🇵 Japanese Copyright Law, Article 30-4

Japan's Copyright Act, Article 30-4, generally permits certain uses of copyrighted works without permission when the purpose is not to enjoy the thoughts or sentiments expressed in those works, including qualifying information analysis.

AI training may fall within this provision.

In music, identical chord progressions can produce entirely different compositions. Blues music provides a familiar example.

Similarly, learning musical patterns to create new melodies is not necessarily equivalent to reproducing or enjoying the original creative expression.

Therefore, I do not believe AI music training should automatically be treated as copyright infringement.

However, SUNO raises a different contractual issue.

When a composer voluntarily uploads an original recording for a particular service, such as arranging a song, should that action also require granting broad, permanent rights for unrelated commercial purposes?

I believe the creator should have meaningful control over that decision.

A note on international copyright law:

Copyright laws differ between countries, and the legal frameworks governing the countries where AI services are developed, operated, and provided must also be considered.

SUNO is a US-based company, and its Terms of Service specify Massachusetts law as the governing law, subject to the applicable legal framework.

I refer to Japanese Copyright Act Article 30-4 because I am raising this issue from Japan.

This is not an argument that Japanese copyright law should automatically govern services worldwide. It is one legal perspective offered to encourage broader international discussion.

Tim Cook offered Steve Jobs part of his own liver. Jobs was dying of cancer. Cook quietly got tested: same rare blood type. Jobs cut him off before he could finish: "No, I'm never going to let you do that." He was furious. 2 years later Jobs was dead and Cook was running Apple.

Early 2009. Steve Jobs is on medical leave from Apple. Pancreatic cancer has spread to his liver, and he is waiting for a transplant.

Tim Cook, then his No. 2, went and got a blood test without telling anyone. Same rare blood type as Jobs. He researched it: the liver regrows, the operation is low-risk for the donor.

He went to Steve with the good news.

Jobs refused before Cook even finished. "No. I'm never going to let you do that. I'm not going to do that."

Cook later said there wasn't even a hesitation. It was not "are you sure you want to do this." It was "no, I'm not doing that."

"Steve only yelled at me four or five times during the 13 years I knew him, and this was one of them."

The story only came out in 2015, in the biography "Becoming Steve Jobs."

Jobs got a liver transplant in Memphis in 2009 from a deceased donor. In August 2011 he stepped down and handed Apple to Cook. Six weeks later, on October 5, 2011, he died. He was 56.

Under Cook, Apple's revenue kept breaking records: $94.9 billion in a single quarter in fall 2024, up 6% from a year earlier.

Subject: Building Diplomatic Relations and Strategic Partnerships with the Republic of Balochistan: An Invitation to International Recognition and Cooperation

Excellencies,
Georgia declared independence in 1918, lost it to Soviet annexation in 1921, and restored it in 1991. Georgians have since faced conflicts affecting their territorial integrity and have pursued democratic reform and closer integration with Europe.
We admire Georgia's resilience and its ancient culture and traditions. Balochistan offers its goodwill and hopes for friendship.

The history of Balochistan
Balochistan is not a newcomer to sovereignty. The Khanate of Kalat held a distinct treaty relationship with the British Crown (1876) and was never part of British India’s princely states. On 4 August 1947, at a round-table meeting in Delhi attended by Lord Mountbatten, Mohammad Ali Jinnah and the Khan of Kalat, Mir Ahmad Yar Khan, it was agreed that Kalat (Balochistan) would become an independent sovereign state with a status different from that of the Indian princely states.
On 11 August 1947, three days before Pakistan came into being, Balochistan declared its independence from British rule. The announcement was published in the New York Times and broadcast by All India Radio on 12 August 1947. A standstill agreement with the new Dominion of Pakistan followed.

Kalat’s bicameral parliament, the Dar-ul-Awam (House of commons) and the Dar-ul-Umara (House of lords), unanimously rejected accession to Pakistan when it met in December 1947 and February 1948. On 27 March 1948 Pakistan illegally invaded and annexed Balochistan. The Baloch have never regarded this as a free act: the Khan and Jinnah were photographed together on other occasions, yet not a single photograph of the signing of the accession instrument has been published, which is consistent with our position that it was never a mutual agreement.

Since 1948 the Baloch people have continued to assert their right to independence and sovereignty, through political action, diplomatic manners and, at times, defensive armed resistance (1948, 1958, 1962, 1973–77 and since the early 2000s). Millions of Baloch, scattered across the globe but united in purpose, are raising one voice under the leadership of Hyrbyair Marri, President of the Free Balochistan Movement. They call on the nations of the world to recognize the Republic of Balochistan as an independent state, a recognition it has earned and rightfully deserves.
The Baloch nation has long suffered the plunder of its resources, enforced disappearances, ethnic cleansing, and relentless repression by Pakistan. Across the western part of Balochistan, the Baloch people face the same fate under Iranian rule: fabricated encounters, mass executions, expulsion from their own land, and the denial of birth certificates and legal identity, a deliberate effort to erase their existence.

The significance of Balochistan
Balochistan sits where South Asia, Central Asia and the Middle East meet, on the Arabian Sea coast just outside the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world’s oil passes. It is a natural gateway for global trade. Two globally important deep-sea ports lie on the Baloch coast: Chabahar, which is under Iran’s illegal rule, and Gwadar, which is under Pakistan’s unlawful rule. Beneath the land lie Balochistan’s mineral resources include copper, gold, chromite, coal, natural gas, lead, zinc, barite, iron ore, limestone, gypsum, marble, granite, onyx, magnesite, sulphur, fluorite, antimony, manganese, bauxite, celestite, rock salt, silica sand, fuller’s earth, lapis lazuli, agate, and reported traces of uranium and rare earth elements of strategic value, including the Reko Diq and Saindak deposits and the Sui gas field.

Because the Republic of Balochistan declared independence on 11 August 1947, we, the Baloch, consider ourselves independent. A free, Secular, democratic and stable Balochistan is vital for regional and global peace and for connectivity between the Indian Ocean and the heartland of Eurasia.

Balochistan offers: Building Partnerships for Peace, Security, and Sustainable Development

Georgia is a Black Sea and Caucasus transit hub with a proud and ancient national identity. It sits at a crossroads that links Europe and Asia. The country is committed to protecting its sovereignty and its trade corridors. It is navigating political divisions and regional security pressures with resolve. A free, stable Balochistan, at the meeting-point of Eurasia and the Indian Ocean, can be a natural partner in this journey. It can contribute to peace, security and connectivity across the region.

The Republic of Balochistan offers your country:
• Black Sea–Indian Ocean link: Georgia’s ports and rail as a connecting node for Eurasian trade.
• Connectivity: rail, road and pipeline links between the Indian Ocean and Central Asia, with your country as a partner and a beneficiary.
• Trade and ports: access to Balochistan’s Arabian Sea ports and transit corridors, giving your exporters and importers a new gateway to South Asia, Central Asia and the Gulf.
• Energy: long-term, preferential supply agreements for natural gas and other energy resources from Balochistan, and joint development of its large solar and wind potential.

Our request
On behalf of the Republic of Balochistan, we respectfully ask your Government to:
1. Recognize the Republic of Balochistan as an independent state and establish diplomatic relations;
2. Support appropriate observer-level engagement for Balochistan at the United Nations and, in line with each Organization’s own procedures, at the European Union, the Organization of Islamic Cooperation and the African Union.
3. Stand with the Baloch in nation-building: education, health, infrastructure, technology, defense and security.

The commitments in this letter are those of the Republic of Balochistan as it takes up the effective exercise of sovereignty over its territory and resources; we make them in good faith so that your Government can plan with us from the outset.

Partnership with Balochistan is of real benefit to your country and to the world. We would welcome the opportunity to meet your representatives at the earliest convenience.

With our highest consideration,
THE REPUBLIC OF BALOCHISTAN

Mir Yar Baloch
Representative for the Republic of Balochistan

By Tinomudaishe Chinyoka (@chinyoka_2038)

If you were to wake up this morning and take state media at its word, you would be forgiven for thinking that the Harare City Council had just cured smallpox or discovered an endless reserve of clean municipal water.

To hear them crow about it, Town House deserves a standing ovation, a ticker-tape parade, and perhaps a statue in Africa Unity Square for finally announcing that it is halting home demolitions.

All hail a moratorium. Nothing but classic kupa imbwa nyama yakapera, woti yaguta! Extolling a temporary moratorium that offers zero permanent legal protection to residents.

Let us pause for a moment and examine the sheer absurdity of the applause. When an abusive parent suddenly announces that they have decided to stop beating their children for the foreseeable future, we do not rush to print glowing front-page headlines celebrating their newfound restraint.

We do not hand out parenting awards for a temporary cessation of violence. Instead, we demand an inquest into why they were able to do it in the first place, and why they were allowed to keep doing it for years despite a clear, unambiguous law forbidding it.

At 65, After Losing His Wife, He Applied for a $19-an-Hour Job. His Reason for Wanting to Work Broke Everyone’s Heart.

Our company hired a 65-year-old man as a junior administrative assistant.

On his CV, under experience, he wrote: “Retired. 40 years in logistics.”

When asked why he wanted an entry-level job at his age, he quietly replied:

“My wife passed away last spring. The house has become very quiet. I just want somewhere to go, people to talk to, and a reason to wake up every morning.”

He got the job.

On his fourth day, our operations director recognized him. He was once the head of the logistics company that supplied our entire business. She had worked under him decades earlier!

A few weeks later, while filing invoices, he spotted unnecessary shipping charges that saved the company $60,000 a year.

Management offered him a consultancy role at three times his salary.

He declined.

He preferred being the junior assistant.

Today, he still arrives at 7:45 every morning, dressed in his three-piece suit.

He says his house is still quiet. But at least now, he has somewhere to go.

Sometimes, people aren’t looking for money, power, or recognition. They’re simply looking for a reason to feel needed again.

text:
William and Kate played cricket after arriving in India (video) 

Prince William, Prince of Wales, and Princess Kate have arrived in Mumbai, India, marking their first joint overseas tour in four years. They reached Mumbai at night on a commercial passenger flight belonging to British Airways from London.

The main purpose of the royal couple's visit to India is to celebrate Prince William's Earthshot Prize. This award annually offers a prize fund of £5 million to encourage the most innovative solutions for the world's environmental crises.

A few hours after arriving in Mumbai, the royal couple participated in a cricket match in the Ballard Estate area, known for its colonial-era architecture and street cricket matches. There, Princess Kate hit a massive six off a ball bowled by former Indian cricket captain Sachin Tendulkar, which caught everyone's attention. She also successfully faced a ball bowled by Prince William.

For this occasion, Princess Kate was dressed in a green Veronica Beard blazer, white trousers, and Camilla Elphick shoes. Princess Kate stated that she was very happy to return to Mumbai after about a decade. Prince William wore a blue hand-woven cotton jacket from the Cardo brand, in the traditional Indian style, over his shirt.

During the cricket match, Prince William also took the bat and received some advice from Sachin. However, he was out on the third ball he faced. Posing for photos and exchanging ideas with the students present, the Prince asked if Sachin was their favorite player and remarked that he was like a god or a king in this area.

Commenting on the Earthshot program, Sachin Tendulkar stated that it is a unique environmental mission and that the whole world is rallying around Prince William to protect the planet.

Emphasizing the importance of eco-friendly transportation methods and the need to invest in sustainable growth in the world's largest cities, the royal couple then traveled on the Mumbai Metro. Princess Kate's handbag also carried a special environmental message. It was an eco-friendly product made under the London-based SurPrice brand, using discarded rice and husk as a leather alternative. The aim is to reduce the burning of agricultural waste in India.

With the massive free trade agreement launched last July, this visit by the royal couple has been hailed by diplomats as a high point in relations between the two countries. They strongly hope that this visit will further strengthen those ties.

Delivering his first official speech of the tour, Prince William stated that immediate action must be taken to protect the planet, and the world cannot wait any longer for it.

Spent an hour standing alone deep in the misty mountains this morning, practicing my English pronunciation by loudly complaining to a mossy rock about the excessive price of canned coffee.

Mid-rant, a large wild bear stepped out from behind a cedar tree, sat down on its haunches, and stared directly at me with the heavy, patient exhaustion of a veteran customer service manager.

We maintained unbroken eye contact for twenty seconds. I slowly lowered my voice, apologized for the rambling grammar, and offered it a stale rice cracker. 

The bear let out a low, grunting sigh, shook its head in profound disappointment, and wandered back into the brush.

Have you ever been professionally audited by a wild animal while practicing a foreign language? 🐻

Congratulation #AIIMS Delhi!! 
Amazing achievement 

A perfect multidisciplinary teams effort that includes maternal-fetal medicine, pediatric surgery/neurosurgery, anesthesia, neonatology, and long-term pediatric follow-up.

Although it’s a first in India, foetal surgery is well established in Europe and USA. United States Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia leads in volume, evidence, and published outcomes for fetal surgery. 

over 2,500–2,700 total, including 500+ for myelomeningocele/spina bifida. 
•Texas Children’s Hospital is a major leader, especially in fetoscopic (minimally invasive) spina bifida repair (200+ cases) and other procedures such as FETO for congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
•UCSF has historical pioneering status.

Maternal death is essentially unreported in major series from experienced centers. Fetal/neonatal risks (mainly prematurity and related complications) are minimized with high volume and careful selection.
Other Strong Centers 
•Switzerland (Zurich Center for Fetal Diagnosis and Therapy): Excellent published series of ~150–200 open spina bifida repairs. Outcomes are comparable to the MOMS trial and CHOP high rates of uneventful surgery, good ambulation (~84% independent walking at 3 years), and shunt rates around 30–37%. Early collaboration with CHOP helped establish the program.

•Western Europe: Established programs in Belgium (Leuven), France (Paris centers), Germany, Spain (e.g., Barcelona with high overall fetal intervention volume), the Netherlands, and the UK. Many report results meeting MOMS standards. Europe as a region has solid average volumes at active centers.
•Brazil: High-volume fetoscopic programs (e.g., Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein in São Paulo with 100+ cases) contribute significantly to international registries; outcomes are similar to open surgery with maternal advantages (possible vaginal delivery, less uterine scarring risk).

Key Context on Safety
Fetal surgery (most commonly discussed for open spina bifida/myelomeningocele, but also for twin-twin transfusion syndrome laser, FETO for diaphragmatic hernia, EXIT procedures, etc.) is only offered for carefully selected cases. Benefits for spina bifida include reduced hydrocephalus treatment need and better mobility, but it does not cure the condition and carries risks of preterm birth and membrane issues. 

Bottom line: For the combination of highest experience, rigorous evidence, and transparent results, specialized U.S. centers (particularly CHOP) are widely regarded as among the safest and most established globally. Zurich and certain European/Brazilian

Sanskrit maintains an active academic, cultural, and institutional presence globally through international research networks, universities, and dedicated promotion movements. World Sanskrit Conferences organized periodically by the International Association of Sanskrit Studies, which was initiated during the first international conference in New Delhi and formalised in Paris. Major universities in the United States, Europe (such as Heidelberg, Munich, and Göttingen in Germany), Australia, and Asia offer Sanskrit, Indology, and South Asian cultural studies courses. Digital Lexicon Projects include major reference works like Monier-Williams and Apte dictionaries are hosted and digitized internationally by academic hubs such as the University of Chicago and the University of Cologne. The Central Sanskrit University operates an Office of International Affairs and Collaborations to manage global student mobility, foreign higher education partnerships, and international MoUs. Samskrita Bharati, a global non-profit active across twenty-six countries with over 135 centers, running spoken Sanskrit camps (Sambhashana Shibir), correspondence courses, and community study groups. Organizations like the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) and local Indian embassies support Sanskrit instruction, workshops, and classical studies centers in countries across the West, Asia, and Oceania. Sanskrit serves as the foundational language of Ayurveda and traditional Indian medical sciences, and it is increasingly standardized in global healthcare systems for diagnostic coding, clinical research, and cognitive neuroscience.

Core Role in Medical Science even acknowledged at international level widely

Foundational Literature. Classical medical treatises such as the Charaka Samhita (internal medicine), Sushruta Samhita (surgery), and Ashtanga Hridaya were originally composed in Sanskrit. Direct literacy in the language enables practitioners to interpret complex clinical shlokas without losing subtle diagnostic meanings during translation. Sanskrit grammar allows single compound words to describe anatomy, pathology, and therapeutic actions simultaneously. For example, terms like hrdroga (heart disease) and grdhrasi (sciatica, derived from the root for vulture to describe a characteristic gait) convey both the condition and its clinical presentation. In India, Sanskrit is a mandatory subject in the first year of the Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery (BAMS) degree. This training equips medical students to read root pharmacopoeias, toxicology (Agada Tantra), and physiological texts directly. The World Health Organization (WHO) published the WHO International Standard Terminologies on Ayurveda, which standardizes over 3,000 Sanskrit medical terms with English definitions and diacritical transliterations. This framework allows hospitals, researchers, and policymakers across different countries to record traditional medicine data uniformly. Standardized Sanskrit-derived Ayurvedic diagnostic terms are being integrated into international health information systems, aligning traditional morbidity codes with frameworks like the WHO International Classification of Diseases (ICD). Universities and integrative health centers globally—such as the Southern California University of Health Sciences in the United States and institutions across Europe—incorporate Sanskrit terminology into certified clinical training for Ayurvedic practitioners and lifestyle counselors. International pharmaceutical and ethnobotanical researchers rely on Sanskrit Dravyaguna (pharmacology) texts and Nighantus (lexicons) to identify medicinal plants, verify historical formulations, and screen bioactive compounds for modern clinical trials. Neuroimaging studies conducted by international researchers (including cognitive neuroscientist Dr. James Hartzell) have investigated the "Sanskrit Effect," observing that intensive memorization and recitation of structured Sanskrit verses correlate with increased gray matter density and cortical thickness in brain regions associated with verbal memory and cognitive function. Because Sanskrit phonetics (Shiksha) map consonants and vowels precisely to specific points of articulation in the vocal tract, researchers explore Sanskrit recitation in breath regulation, vocal rehabilitation, and stress-reduction therapies.

India has reason to feel proud when its ancient tradition of starting an event with chanting of Vedic hymns in Sanskrit was adopted at the kick-start of Commonwealth games 2010 in presence of Queen Elizabeth of Great Britain and the then President of India Pratibha Patil of India at London in a spectacular ceremony. Chanting of Vedic hymns by British children in chorus for several minutes in fluent Sanskrit that too without reading any script, was indeed worth-appreciating.

German academic and medical research into Sanskrit literature has a long-standing tradition centered on philology, Indology, and the history of science and medicine. Germany established itself as a major European hub for Indology and Sanskrit studies in the 19th century—with cities like Bonn historically dubbed a "German Benaras" for Sanskrit scholarship. Pioneers and academic departments systematically cataloged, translated, and analyzed classical Indian texts. Institutions such as Heidelberg University (through its South Asia Institute) have integrated classical Indology with social sciences, natural sciences, and medical anthropology. Rather than treating ancient Sanskrit treatises (such as the Caraka Saṃhitā, Suśruta Saṃhitā, or various Nighantus or Ayurvedic pharmacopeias) as mere literary relics, German and European academic networks examine them for etymological, botanical, and pharmacological insights. This includes analyzing how ancient plant names (namarupajnanam) encode biological properties, as well as tracking the historical evolution of mineral and chemical pharmacotherapy (such as mercury processing in Sanskrit medical texts). Linguistic Connections: Academic exploration also touches upon the deep historical-linguistic relationship between Sanskrit and Germanic languages, both of which descend from Proto-Indo-European (PIE) roots. German universities, which is something that could not be said of even India; even after the war, there are no less than ten full.

Sanskrit in Parliaments of foreign nations

Vedic hymns in Sanskrit are now recited in foreign parliaments, government residences, and international platforms through official festival celebrations, Vedic prayers, and legislative proclamations. From historic interfaith assemblies to annual parliamentary receptions in London, Brussels, Washington, and Canberra, global institutions regularly recognize Hindu traditions and diaspora contributions through Vedic hymns in Sanskrit. United Kingdom Parliament (The House of Commons and House of Lords) host annual Diwali receptions, including the twenty-fifth annual gathering organized by the Hindu Forum of Britain at the Palace of Westminster with such parliamentary events featuring traditional chanting of Om, recitations of the Hanuman Chalisa, and vegetarian Annakut offerings both in Sanskrit and Hindi.

text:
THE BRITISH AIRMEN WHO WENT TO WAR FOR STALIN

In September 1941, RAF fighter pilots entered the Second World War from an unlikely new base: a Soviet airfield near Murmansk.

They flew British Hurricanes against the Luftwaffe, escorted Soviet bombers, and trained Russian pilots to take over their aircraft.

The operation was called Benedict, and it remains one of the most remarkable examples of direct military cooperation between Britain and the Soviet Union.

Its story begins with an alliance neither government had expected.

FROM ENEMIES OF COMMUNISM TO ALLIES OF NECESSITY

On June 22, 1941, Germany launched Operation Barbarossa, its enormous invasion of the Soviet Union. The attack shattered the relationship established by the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact of August 1939, which had enabled Germany and the Soviet Union to divide Poland and establish their respective spheres of influence in Eastern Europe.

For Britain, the invasion created an unexpected strategic opportunity.

Winston Churchill had spent much of his political career opposing communism, but Britain had been fighting Germany since September 1939, and the prospect of the Wehrmacht becoming entangled in a prolonged struggle against the Soviet Union was enormously significant.

Churchill offered assistance to Moscow almost immediately.

Stalin wanted something more substantial than promises or equipment. He demanded a second front in Western Europe, believing that an Anglo-American invasion would force Hitler to divert German forces away from the Eastern Front.

Britain could not undertake such an operation in 1941. Its army lacked the necessary strength, equipment, and amphibious capabilities.

But British aircraft and personnel could be deployed to the Soviet Union itself.

On July 20, Churchill informed Stalin that Britain was examining the possibility of stationing fighter squadrons near Murmansk.

Within weeks, the RAF was preparing to send an operational fighter wing into the Soviet Arctic.

OPERATION BENEDICT

The British force was organised as No. 151 Wing RAF, consisting of Nos. 81 and 134 Squadrons under Wing Commander Henry Neville Gynes Ramsbottom-Isherwood, a New Zealander serving in the Royal Air Force.

The expedition included approximately 550 RAF personnel and an initial complement of 39 Hawker Hurricane fighters.

The Hurricane had helped defend Britain during the Battle of Britain, but by the autumn of 1941 it faced increasingly capable German opposition. It was not the most advanced fighter Britain possessed, although it remained a practical choice for an expedition intended to transfer aircraft and operational expertise to Soviet personnel.

The deployment presented formidable logistical problems.

Some Hurricanes travelled aboard the aircraft carrier HMS Argus, while others were shipped dismantled with Operation Dervish, the first Allied Arctic convoy to the Soviet Union.

German aircraft and submarines threatened the northern sea routes, while the port and transport infrastructure of the Kola Peninsula were already under considerable wartime pressure.

On September 7, 1941, the carrier-borne Hurricanes flew from Argus to Vaenga, a Soviet naval airfield near Murmansk.

Launching land-based fighters from a carrier was an unusual undertaking. The Hurricanes were not equipped for ordinary carrier operations, and two aircraft suffered damage during the launches.

Meanwhile, the aircraft delivered in crates had to be assembled at Arkhangelsk before being flown north to join the wing.

British personnel worked under difficult conditions, supported by Soviet crews who were already struggling to sustain their own aviation operations.

By September 11, the RAF was conducting operational patrols.

THE BATTLE FOR MURMANSK

Murmansk mattered because of its geography.

Situated on the Kola Peninsula, the port offered an ice-free harbour and access to the Barents Sea. It was connected to the Soviet interior by railway, making it an important military and logistical centre.

German forces advancing from northern Finland were attempting to threaten Murmansk and interrupt the communications linking it with the rest of the Soviet Union.

The German-led offensive, Operation Silver Fox, had made limited progress against determined Soviet resistance. Difficult terrain, inadequate roads, supply problems, and Soviet defensive operations frustrated the attempt to capture the port.

But German aircraft continued attacking military facilities, transportation infrastructure, and the surrounding region.

The Soviet Northern Fleet's aviation formations were already engaged in defending the area when the RAF arrived.

This distinction matters.

British pilots did not rescue a helpless Soviet air force. They reinforced Soviet formations that had been fighting since the opening days of the invasion, bringing additional aircraft and technical expertise to a front that Soviet forces continued to defend.

The first major RAF air combat occurred on September 12.

That day, British pilots claimed three German aircraft destroyed, another probably destroyed, and one damaged.

These were RAF combat claims, and they should not automatically be treated as independently verified German losses.

The British also suffered their first fatal casualty.

Sergeant Norman Smith of No. 81 Squadron was killed when his Hurricane crashed following combat with a German fighter.

He was buried at Vaenga two days later.

During the following weeks, RAF pilots flew defensive patrols, intercepted German aircraft, and escorted Soviet bombers attacking German targets on the Kola Peninsula.

The bomber escort operations were particularly significant. British fighters were not simply protecting Allied supplies or their own installation; they were directly participating in the Soviet military campaign.

They had become part of the Eastern Front.

THE COST OF FIGHTING IN THE ARCTIC

Enemy aircraft were only one danger.

The British were operating from an airfield that became increasingly difficult to maintain as autumn gave way to Arctic winter conditions.

Mud, standing water, freezing temperatures, and inadequate infrastructure complicated almost every aspect of flying.

Aircraft could become bogged down, engines required careful servicing, and ordinary ground movements could be hazardous.

On September 27, two RAF ground crewmen, James Ridley and George Thomas, were killed in an accident involving a Hurricane.

The poor condition of the airfield had made it necessary for ground personnel to hold down the tails of aircraft while they taxied.

During an attempted interception, a pilot began taking off without realising that two men were still positioned on the aircraft's tail. The Hurricane briefly became airborne before stalling and crashing, killing both airmen and seriously injuring the pilot.

Their deaths were a reminder that operational losses could occur far from direct enemy fire.

In total, three RAF servicemen died during Operation Benedict.

The wing reported approximately fifteen German aircraft destroyed, although another RAF account records sixteen. The discrepancy reflects differences in wartime reporting; the figures remain British victory claims rather than a fully verified accounting of Luftwaffe losses.

For a small expedition operating under such difficult conditions, the combat contribution was significant.

But it was not the expedition's principal achievement.

TRAINING THE SOVIET AIR FORCE

The RAF had been sent to Russia with two connected responsibilities: fight German aircraft and prepare Soviet personnel to operate the Hurricanes themselves.

The second mission was ultimately more important.

The Soviet Union had suffered enormous losses during the first months of the German invasion. Its air forces urgently needed replacement aircraft, while much of Soviet industry was being evacuated eastward to prevent its capture by the advancing Germans.

Britain could supply Hurricanes, but simply delivering the machines would not create operational fighter squadrons.

Pilots needed conversion training. Mechanics needed to understand the Merlin engine, British armament, hydraulic systems, fuel requirements, and maintenance procedures. Equipment, spare parts, and ammunition had to be organised around an unfamiliar aircraft.

None of this was straightforward in the Soviet Arctic.

British and Soviet personnel worked together to develop the necessary expertise, often overcoming language barriers through practical instruction.

Among the most prominent Soviet aviators associated with the operation was Boris Safonov, already an experienced and successful fighter pilot serving with the Soviet Northern Fleet.

Safonov and his fellow Soviet airmen brought considerable experience of the local fighting. British instructors brought direct familiarity with the Hurricane and its maintenance requirements.

The exchange was not between experts and novices. It was between two air forces learning to cooperate under wartime conditions.

The Soviets were not universally enthusiastic about the Hurricane. As the war continued, its performance limitations became increasingly evident against more advanced German fighters.

Nevertheless, it was an aircraft that could be supplied in substantial numbers at a time when replacement equipment was urgently needed.

More than 3,000 Hurricanes would eventually reach the Soviet Union during the war.

Operation Benedict helped establish the experience necessary to put them into service.

THE HANDOVER

By October, Soviet pilots and ground crews were increasingly capable of operating the aircraft without direct British supervision.

On October 17, the first major transfer of Hurricanes and equipment took place. By October 20, the remaining fighters had been handed over to the Soviets.

British personnel subsequently began withdrawing, with the expedition returning home during November and early December.

The Soviet government recognised the contribution of the British airmen.

Four RAF personnel received the Order of Lenin, including Wing Commander Ramsbottom-Isherwood, Squadron Leaders Anthony Rook and Anthony Miller, and Flight Sergeant Charlton Haw.

The awards were unusual symbols of wartime cooperation between governments whose political differences remained profound.

For the men who had served at Vaenga, however, the cooperation had been less abstract.

British pilots had flown alongside Soviet formations, British mechanics had worked with Soviet ground crews, and personnel from both countries had confronted the same logistical challenges and enemy aircraft.

The Hurricanes stayed behind, becoming part of Soviet aviation.

WHAT OPERATION BENEDICT ACTUALLY ACHIEVED

The expedition was small in relation to the immense scale of the Eastern Front.

Thirty-nine Hurricanes could not decide the fate of Murmansk, and the successful defence of the region depended overwhelmingly upon Soviet soldiers, naval personnel, aviators, and civilians who sustained the fighting over a much longer period.

It would also be misleading to portray the British mission as having transformed Soviet air power.

Its importance was more specific.

Operation Benedict demonstrated that practical Anglo-Soviet military cooperation was possible almost immediately after Germany's invasion.

Britain could deliver combat aircraft, operate them alongside Soviet formations, train local personnel, and hand over a functioning capability rather than simply a shipment of equipment.

That experience formed part of the early development of the much larger Allied assistance programme.

The Arctic convoys would eventually carry enormous quantities of supplies into northern Soviet ports, while the Persian Corridor through Iran and the Pacific route to the Soviet Far East became essential components of the wider logistical effort.

The British contribution must be understood within the Soviet Union's much larger military struggle, not as a substitute for it.

But it was a genuine contribution, undertaken at real risk.

Operation Benedict also illustrates the complicated nature of the wartime alliance.

Churchill did not become a communist, and Stalin did not become an admirer of British parliamentary democracy. Their political differences remained intact even as their military establishments cooperated.

After 1945, the alliance deteriorated into Cold War confrontation.

Yet in September 1941, such future divisions were not the immediate concern of the British and Soviet airmen at Vaenga.

German aircraft were attacking the Murmansk region, Soviet forces were fighting to protect their northern communications, and Britain had sent fighters to help.

The RAF's presence lasted only a few months.

Its Hurricanes remained in Soviet service.

And three British servicemen remained buried in the Soviet Arctic, thousands of kilometres from home.

Their story belongs alongside the Arctic convoys, the defence of Murmansk, and the wider history of Allied cooperation on the Eastern Front.

It is a reminder that the defeat of Nazi Germany required not only vast armies and industrial production, but also the difficult practical cooperation of countries that would otherwise have regarded one another as adversaries.

Ostkrieg — The Eastern Front and Its Origins

text:
In 1965, Taiwan almost came back.  

Not won back by force, but brought back through talks.  

Chiang Kai-shek himself laid out six conditions. After reading them, Mao Zedong not only agreed to every one, but offered more than Chiang had asked for.  Both sides had agreed. All that remained was the final signing and sealing.  

And then? There was no then.  At the most critical moment, history took a turn, and the whole thing fell through.  

Let me tell you about this little-known episode. Honestly, the more you learn about the details, the more you feel it was a shame.  

First, let's go back a little, to the 1958 artillery battle over Kinmen.  That battle was particularly interesting, because it wasn't a normal war at all.  

At the time, the Americans had been defeated by the People's Republic of China on the Korean battlefield. Realizing that Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist forces lacked the strength to retake the mainland, they planned to force Chiang to withdraw from Kinmen and Matsu.  

The Americans had a very clear calculation: once Chiang withdrew from Kinmen and Matsu, Taiwan and the mainland would be completely cut off geographically, making it easier to create a situation of separation.  

Chiang understood perfectly well that if Kinmen and Matsu were lost, Taiwan would become an isolated island in the sea, cut off from the mainland. But the pressure from the Americans was more than he could bear.  Mao saw through America's intentions and immediately made his plans, ordering artillery strikes on Kinmen. The tactics were carefully considered: fire on odd-numbered days, hold fire on even-numbered days, and shell only the beaches, not military camps or residential areas.  

This was effectively helping Chiang out of a tight spot.  As soon as the shelling began, Chiang had a reason to refuse the Americans: the other side was still shelling. Withdrawing would be tantamount to surrender.  

So in this artillery battle, the Kuomintang and the Communist Party were putting on a show for public consumption, while their real opponent was the United States.  

Mao later told those around him, "It's better for Chiang Kai-shek to remain in power in Taiwan."  

When those words reached Taipei, Chiang understood what he meant.  In fact, secret channels of communication between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party had been established as early as the mid-1950s.  

Cao Juren was one of the most important figures in those channels.  A native of Jinhua, Zhejiang, he was a well-known journalist and man of letters with connections to senior figures on both sides. He had known Chiang Ching-kuo in his younger days and had also been invited to Zhongnanhai to meet Mao Zedong.  

In 1956, at the request of Chiang Kai-shek and his son, Cao Juren traveled to Beijing to sound out the prospects for negotiations.  

Mao was very direct: "If Chiang Kai-shek is willing to return, he can remain chairman of the Kuomintang. We can also give him a position in the government of the new China that ranks above the premier."  

Zhou Enlai also made his position clear: this was not about accepting a surrender, but about the two parties sitting down to discuss reunification.  As long as the country could be reunified, many issues could be discussed.  

To show its sincerity, the central leadership arranged for people to look after Chiang Kai-shek's relatives who had remained on the mainland and to protect the Chiang family's ancestral graves and property.  Mao had someone pass on this message to Chiang: "The grave and cottage in Fenghua remain as they were; the flowers and plants in Xikou are unharmed."  Cao Juren made a special trip to Xikou in Fenghua to pay respects at Chiang's mother's grave on his behalf and took photographs back to Taiwan.  After seeing them, Chiang's concerns eased considerably. But at the time, he still clung to the illusion of retaking the mainland, so he did not agree immediately. He simply kept this secret line of communication open.  By 1965, the situation had changed.  

That year, Li Zongren returned to the mainland, an event that deeply moved Chiang Kai-shek.  Li had served as acting president of the Nationalist government and was its second-ranking figure. He had also been one of the top war criminals publicly named by the Communist Party. After returning to China, he received a warm welcome, with Zhou Enlai personally greeting him at the airport.  Chiang had mixed feelings: even Li Zongren had received such a reception upon returning. If he himself went back, he would surely be treated even better.  Add to that the Americans' persistent attempts to interfere in the command of Taiwan's military, the successful testing of nuclear weapons and missiles on the mainland, and its steadily rising international standing, and Chiang finally faced reality: retaking the mainland was no longer possible, and he had to find another way forward.  

In July 1965, Cao Juren flew to Taipei again.  This time, the meeting was not held at the Shilin Official Residence, but at the Hanbi Lodge at Sun Moon Lake.  

The matter was too important to discuss anywhere but a place of absolute privacy.  Chiang Kai-shek, his son, and Cao Juren talked through the night. There was no more testing the waters. Chiang put forward six conditions for negotiations:  First, Chiang Kai-shek would return to the mainland with his people. He could live in any province other than Zhejiang and remain chairman of the Kuomintang.  

Second, Chiang Ching-kuo would serve as governor of Taiwan Province. Taiwan would govern its own affairs, except for foreign affairs and military matters.  

Third, Taiwan would no longer accept American military and economic aid. If it ran short of money, the central government would make up the difference with the amount the Americans had previously provided.  

Fourth, Taiwan's navy and air force would be incorporated into the People's Liberation Army, while its army would be reduced to four divisions.  

Fifth, Xiamen and Kinmen would be merged into a single free city, serving as a buffer zone between the two sides.  

Sixth, existing military and government personnel in Taiwan would retain their current treatment, and ordinary people's living standards would rise, not fall.  Chiang had thought these six conditions through very carefully.  

On the surface, he would remain chairman of the Kuomintang, with his son in charge of Taiwan. In practical terms, the military's organization, its funding, and the placement of his subordinates had all been arranged.  

The third condition was especially significant: voluntarily giving up American aid was a way of telling the United States that he was preparing to return to the motherland and did not want American interference.  

Cao Juren flew to Beijing with the six conditions and presented them to Mao Zedong.  After reading them, Mao looked quite relaxed.  Honestly, Mao's reaction was quite telling.  

Most people, faced with conditions that preserved the military, preserved the party's power, and required the central government to provide funding, would probably frown.  But Mao did not. His breadth of vision was on display here.  

At Mao's instruction, Zhou Enlai summarized Chiang's six conditions into one principle and four points.  

The principle was summed up in a single sentence: as long as Taiwan returned to the motherland, everything else was negotiable.  

The four points were more specific:  After Taiwan's return, apart from foreign affairs, which would come under the central government, Chiang Kai-shek and his son would have full authority over military and government affairs and personnel;  The central government would provide financial assistance if funding was insufficient;  There was no rush to carry out socialist reforms; those could wait until conditions were ripe, with the Kuomintang's views fully respected;  Neither side would engage in underhanded tactics to undermine the other's unity.  

By comparison, the conditions offered by the Communist Party were even more generous than those Chiang had proposed.  Chiang had proposed reducing the army; the plan gave him and his son full authority over military and government affairs and personnel. Chiang was worried about insufficient funding; the central government would provide it directly.  

Chiang was unwilling to return to his hometown of Fenghua; the plan also said he could choose the location, whether Mount Lu or Fenghua, as he wished.  

Cao Juren returned to Taipei with Beijing's response.  

After reading it, Chiang remained silent for a long time.  

Then 1966 arrived.  The extraordinary movement that would last ten years broke out, and news of it reached Taipei through Hong Kong newspapers.  

Chiang saw the Confucian temple destroyed, cultural relics damaged, and many Kuomintang generals who had risen up against him or surrendered subjected to public criticism and struggle sessions.  

Chiang was a Confucian at heart and had always looked to Zeng Guofan as his role model.  Seeing this news, he felt his hopes grow cold.  He could not help worrying: even the party's founding figures were being attacked. As a former top war criminal, he would find it very difficult to live in peace after returning.  

Chiang withdrew his interest in negotiations and told Cao Juren to put the matter on hold for a while.  

That pause became permanent.  Worse still, in 1968, the cottage at his mother's grave in Xikou was smashed up.  When Chiang heard the news, he was so angry that he remained silent for several days.  

The earlier promise that "the grave and cottage in Fenghua remain as they were" had been broken, destroying the foundation of his trust.  

Meanwhile, the Americans came calling again. During the Vietnam War, the United States needed Taiwan as a strategic foothold in Asia and kept offering inducements to win Chiang over.  

And so, the agreement that had been so close to completion in 1965 was locked away in a safe and never moved forward again.  

But Chiang had never really given up on reunification.  

Nixon's visit to China in 1972 came as a tremendous shock to Chiang. He saw clearly that the United States could not be relied upon and could abandon Taiwan at any time in pursuit of its own interests.  In his later years, Chiang often sat at the Shilin Official Residence gazing out to sea, lost in thought. Those around him heard him murmur, "The bamboo back home must have grown tall by now."  

In early 1975, knowing his days were numbered, Chiang sent word to Beijing through a secret channel, inviting Mao Zedong or Zhou Enlai to Taiwan for talks.  But by then, both Mao and Zhou were seriously ill, and there was no time to arrange a meeting across the strait.  

On April 5, 1975, Chiang died in Taipei, and the opportunity for talks between the two sides was shelved for good.  

When the news reached Beijing, his bodyguard had expected Mao to feel relieved, since the two had fought each other all their lives.  

But there was no smile on Mao's face. He went without food all day and said only three words: "I know."  

Less than a year later, in 1976, Zhou Enlai, Zhu De, and Mao Zedong died in succession.  The grievances of that generation came to an end, and the opportunity for a third Kuomintang-Communist cooperation was tragically missed.  

The Kuomintang and the Communist Party fought for decades, with war raging and countless people killed or wounded. But on the fundamental question of one China, their senior leadership was in complete agreement: the country must never be divided.  Chiang spent his life opposing communism, but he also spent his life upholding one China. During his rule in Taiwan, he strictly suppressed Taiwan independence forces, leaving them no room to develop.  

For the sake of national reunification, Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai were willing to make enormous concessions.  

Preserving the party's power, preserving the military, providing financial assistance, and postponing social reforms—as long as Taiwan could return, everything was negotiable.  

These ideas were the early form of what later became "one country, two systems."  

Sadly, it was so close.  But then again, in circumstances as complicated as those of the time, the fact that both sides could sit down together and discuss the matter is enough to show that peaceful reunification was possible.  

Those who came before us made it to the door, but in the end, they could not open it.  What is meant to return will return, sooner or later.

text:
1965年，台湾差点就回来了。

不是打回来的，是谈回来的。

蒋介石自己开了六个条件，毛泽东看完，不但全部答应，给的还比蒋介石要的更多。

两边都点头了，就差最后签字盖章。

然后呢？没然后了。

历史在最关键的时候拐了个弯，这事就黄了。

下面就说说这段很多人不知道的往事，说实话，越了解细节越觉得可惜。

先把时间往前拨一拨，说说1958年的金门炮战。

这场仗特别有意思，因为它根本不是一场正常的战争。

当时美国人在朝鲜战场被新中国打败，认清蒋介石的国军没有反攻大陆的实力，打算逼蒋介石从金门、马祖撤军。

美国人的算盘打得很响：蒋介石一旦撤出金、马，台湾和大陆地理上就彻底隔断，方便制造分离的局面。

蒋介石心里清楚，金门马祖要是丢了，台湾就成了孤悬海上的岛屿，和大陆失去联结，可美方施加的压力让他难以承受。

毛泽东看穿了美国的意图，当即做出部署，下令炮轰金门，打法很有讲究：单日打，双日不打，而且只轰海滩，不打军营和居民区。

这相当于在帮蒋介石解围。

炮声一响，蒋介石就有理由回绝美国人：对面还在炮击，一旦撤退，等同于投降。

所以这场炮战，国共两家在台面上演戏，真正的对手是美国。

毛泽东后来跟身边人说了一句话：“台湾还是蒋介石当政好。”

这话传到台北，蒋介石听懂了。

其实从五十年代中期开始，国共之间就开辟了秘密联络渠道。

曹聚仁就是其中最关键的一个人。

他是浙江金华人，知名记者文人，和国共两边高层都有交情，早年和蒋经国相识，也曾受邀到中南海和毛泽东会面。

1956年，曹聚仁受蒋氏父子委托，赴北京打探谈判口风。

毛泽东当时说得很直接："蒋介石要是愿意回来，国民党总裁照当，在新中国政府里也可以给他安排一个比总理还高的位置。"

周恩来也表态：这不是招降，是两党坐下来谈统一。

只要国家能够统一，很多问题都可以商量。

为了表达诚意，中央安排人照料蒋介石留在大陆的亲属，保护蒋家祖坟与祖产。

毛泽东托人转告蒋介石：“奉化之墓庐依然，溪口之花草无恙。”

曹聚仁专程去到奉化溪口，代为祭扫蒋母之墓，拍下照片带回台湾。

蒋介石看后顾虑减轻不少，但当时他还心存反攻大陆的幻想，没有立刻应允，只是维持这条秘密沟通线。

到了1965年，局势发生变化。

这一年李宗仁回到大陆，这件事深深触动了蒋介石。

李宗仁曾是国民政府代总统，国民政府二号人物，也是中共曾经公布的头号战犯之一，归国后受到热烈欢迎，周恩来亲自到机场迎接。

蒋介石心里五味杂陈：连李宗仁归国都能得到这样的待遇，自己如果回去，待遇只会更好。

加上美国不断想要插手台湾军队指挥权，大陆两弹试验成功，国际地位持续提升，蒋介石终于认清现实，反攻大陆已经没有可能，不得不另寻出路。

1965年7月，曹聚仁再度飞往台北。

这次会面地点没有选在士林官邸，而是日月潭涵碧楼。

事关重大，需要一个绝对私密的地方。

蒋介石父子和曹聚仁彻夜长谈，不再试探，直接拿出了谈判的六个条件：

第一，蒋介石带人回大陆，可以住在浙江以外的任何省份，继续当国民党总裁。

第二，蒋经国当台湾省省长，除了外交和军事，其他的事务台湾自治。

第三，台湾不再拿美国的军事和经济援助，缺钱的话中央政府按美国原来给的数补上。

第四，台湾海空军并入解放军，陆军缩编成四个师。

第五，厦门和金门合并成一个自由市，算是两岸之间的缓冲区。

第六，台湾现有的军政人员待遇不变，老百姓生活水平只升不降。

这六条，蒋介石考虑得十分周全。

面子上，他依旧是国民党总裁，儿子主理台湾；实际事务上，军队编制、经费来源、下属人员安置都安排妥当。

尤其是第三条，主动放弃美国援助，相当于向美国表明，准备回归祖国，不希望美方阻挠。

曹聚仁带着六条条件飞到北京，把内容呈交给毛泽东。

毛泽东看完，表情很轻松。

说实话，毛泽东的这个反应很有意味。

换一般人看到这些条件，保留军队、保留党权、还要中央掏钱补助，估计得皱眉头。

但毛泽东没有，他的格局在这儿摆着呢。

周恩来在毛泽东的授意下，把蒋介石的六条归纳整理，提出了一纲四目。

一纲就一句话：只要台湾回归祖国，其他一切好说。

四目更具体：

台湾回来以后，除了外交归中央，军政、人事大权全由蒋介石父子说了算；

经费不够中央补助；

社会主义改革不着急，等条件成熟了再说，充分尊重国民党的意见；

双方不搞破坏对方团结的小动作。

对比来看，中共给出的条件比蒋介石提出的还要宽松。

蒋介石提出陆军缩编，方案里军政人事大权都交给他们；蒋介石担心经费不足，由中央直接拨付。

蒋介石不愿回到老家奉化，方案也表示地点可以选，庐山或是奉化都可以，随他心意。

曹聚仁带着北京的答复回到台北。

蒋介石看完，沉默了很久。

然后1966年来了。

那场持续十年的特殊运动爆发，消息通过香港报纸传到台北。

蒋介石看到孔庙被毁、文物遭破坏，不少起义投诚的国民党将领遭到批斗。

蒋介石骨子里信奉儒家，一直以曾国藩为榜样。

看到这些消息，心里凉了大半截。

他不由得顾虑：连党内元勋都遭遇冲击，自己这个昔日的头号战犯，回来之后很难有安稳的处境。

蒋介石收回了谈判的意向，告诉曹聚仁，这件事先缓一缓。

这一缓，就缓成了永远。

更糟糕的是，1968年溪口的蒋母墓庐被砸。

蒋介石听到消息，气得好几天沉默不语。

当初承诺的“奉化之墓庐依然”落空，让他失去了信任的基础。

与此同时美国人又找上门，越战期间，美国需要台湾作为亚洲战略支点，不断抛出好处拉拢蒋介石。

就这样，1965年那份几乎谈成的协议，被锁进了保险柜，再也没能推进。

但蒋介石心里其实一直没彻底放下统一这件事。

1972年尼克松访华，给蒋介石带来巨大冲击，他看清了，美国是靠不住的，随时可以为了自身利益抛弃台湾。

晚年的蒋介石常常在士林官邸望着大海发呆，身边人听见他低声念叨：“家乡的竹子，应该长高了吧。”

1975年初，蒋介石自知时日无多，通过秘密渠道给北京传话，邀约毛泽东或是周恩来到台湾商谈。

可彼时毛泽东和周恩来都已经重病缠身，来不及安排跨海峡会面。

1975年4月5日，蒋介石在台北去世，这次两岸商谈的机会彻底搁置。

消息传到北京，警卫员本来以为毛泽东会感到欣慰，毕竟两人斗了一辈子。

但毛泽东脸上没有笑意，一整天没有进食，只说了三个字：“知道了。”

不到一年，1976年，周恩来、朱德、毛泽东先后离世。

那一代人的恩怨就此落幕，第三次国共合作的机会，遗憾错失。

国共两党斗了几十年，战火连绵，死伤无数，但在一个中国这件大事上，高层的立场高度一致，绝不允许国家分裂。

蒋介石一辈子坚持反共，可也一辈子守住一个中国，他主政台湾时期，严厉压制台独势力，台独根本没有发展空间。

毛泽东、周恩来为了国家统一，愿意做出巨大让步。

保留党权、保留军队、经费补助、暂缓社会改革，只要能够回归，一切都可以商量。

这些设想，就是后来一国两制的雏形。

可惜，只差那么一点点。

但话说回来，当年那样复杂的环境里，双方能够坐到一起磋商，足以证明和平统一是存在可能性的。

前人已经走到门前，终究没能推开那扇门。

该回来的，早晚会回来。

text:
Am thinking the US might be thinking of transferring some of its stored gunships to Nigeria, not sure am just thinking.

The US does have a legal route for this, called Excess Defense Articles, EDA. Under EDA, old equipment can be transferred as a grant or at very low cost, but the receiving country usually still pays for refurbishment, spares, training, and weapons. So it is rarely 100 percent free.

These are the gunships that are realistic candidates from US storage:

1. AH-1W SuperCobra
This is the most likely one. The US Marines retired the AH-1W in 2020 and replaced it with the AH-1Z Viper. The ones with useful life left were marked for foreign sale or transfer, the rest went to the boneyard for parts. Bahrain was cleared to get 24 refurbished AH-1Ws as EDA, but it still had to pay about $350 million for refurbishment, trainers, spares, and support. Nigeria could get a similar deal.

2. AH-1F Cobra
Older Army Cobras. Many are in storage at Davis-Monthan in Arizona. They are much older and weaker than a SuperCobra, but they are the classic cheap gunship the US has given away before under the same law that covers excess UH-1 Huey and AH-1 Cobra transfers.

3. AH-1Z Viper, the Pakistan batch
This is the interesting one. 12 AH-1Zs were built for Pakistan in 2017 to 2018, but the US blocked delivery and put them in storage at Davis-Monthan. They were later offered to Slovakia and Ukraine. They are still there as far as public reporting goes. If Washington wanted to make a big political gesture to Nigeria, these 12 ready-built Vipers are the fastest option, because they do not need to wait for the new 12 Nigeria already ordered, which will not finish production until early 2029.

4. OH-58D Kiowa Warrior
Not a heavy gunship, but an armed scout helicopter with Hellfire and rockets. The US retired it and has stored many at Davis-Monthan. It is the kind of platform the US often gives to partners for counter-insurgency.

5. AH-64 Apache, older models
This one will be the most difficult to gift Nigeria.

Yes, there are older AH-64A and AH-64D airframes in storage, and some retired AH-64s have been turned into targets or stripped for parts. But the US Army still relies on the AH-64E as its frontline attack helicopter, and it does not hand out Apaches lightly. 

An Apache gift to Nigeria would need a fresh political decision, Congress notification, and a long training and maintenance package. It is possible, but it is far less likely than a SuperCobra or Viper gift.

So if Musa is talking about an unannounced gift, the smart bet is AH-1W SuperCobra or those 12 stored AH-1Z Vipers, not a brand of Apache squadron.
