text:
The Beginning of Sorrows:

Jesus never said the end-time signs would all come at once.

He said they would come like labor pains.

Every mother reading this knows what that means. Once you see it, you will never read Matthew 24 the same way again.

Read to the end, and check every verse. I want you to.

THE WORDS OF JESUS

“And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places. All these are the beginning of sorrows.” (Matthew 24:6-8)

The word translated “sorrows” is the Greek word ōdin (Strong’s G5604). It means birth pangs. Labor pains.

Jesus chose that word on purpose. Think about what labor pains do:

They start small. “The beginning of sorrows” (Matthew 24:8)
They grow stronger. “For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world” (Matthew 24:21)
Once they start, nothing stops them. “Shall I bring to the birth, and not cause to bring forth? saith the LORD” (Isaiah 66:9)
They end in a birth. “As soon as she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish” (John 16:21)

THE PROPHETS SAW IT FIRST

Isaiah tied labor pains to the Day of the LORD: “Howl ye; for the day of the LORD is at hand... they shall be in pain as a woman that travaileth” (Isaiah 13:6, 8). Two verses later the sun is darkened (Isaiah 13:10).

Jeremiah saw strong men holding themselves “as a woman in travail,” and he called it the time of Jacob’s trouble: “Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.” (Jeremiah 30:6-7)

Isaiah also showed where the labor leads: “Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs” (Isaiah 26:17). Then comes this: “Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise.” (Isaiah 26:19)

First the pangs, then the resurrection.

Even the ancient Jewish sages knew this teaching. The Talmud calls this season the “birth pangs of the Messiah” (Sanhedrin 98b). Some rabbis dreaded it so much they said, “Let him come, but let me not see him.”

THE ORDER JESUS GAVE

Read Matthew 24 slowly and you’ll see the labor has stages.

Early labor: deception, wars, famines, earthquakes. “The beginning of sorrows.” (Matthew 24:4-8)

Hard labor: the abomination of desolation stands in the holy place, “for then shall be great tribulation.” (Matthew 24:15, 21)

The final push: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened.” (Matthew 24:29)

The birth: “they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect.” (Matthew 24:30-31)

Notice the order. The tribulation comes first, then the signs in the sky, then the trumpet and the gathering.

WHO GETS CAUGHT OFF GUARD?

Paul used the same picture: “For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.” (1 Thessalonians 5:3)

Now read the next verse. It changes everything: “But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief.” (1 Thessalonians 5:4)

And then: “For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ.” (1 Thessalonians 5:9)

The labor overtakes a sleeping world. It does not have to surprise you.

HOW LONG IS THE LABOR?

Here I am going to be careful, because I want you to test this, not take my word for it.

I have been studying the patterns in Scripture, and I want to suggest a possible timeline. What follows is my own reading. These dates are not written in the Bible, so test every step.

A human pregnancy is about 40 weeks. The Jubilee is a 50-year unit (Leviticus 25:10). 40 x 50 = 2,000 years of labor.

“One day is with the Lord as a thousand years” (2 Peter 3:8). “After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up” (Hosea 6:2). Two days = 2,000 years from the resurrection. Many scholars date the crucifixion to AD 30, and AD 30 + 2,000 = 2030.

Jesus said, “Now learn a parable of the fig tree... This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled” (Matthew 24:32-34). On January 23, 1950, Israel’s Knesset proclaimed Jerusalem its capital. Then Psalm 90:10 says: “if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” 1950 + 80 = 2030.

Daniel 12:11 gives 1,290 days from the time the daily sacrifice is taken away and the abomination is set up. I believe the abomination may take place at Firstfruits, at sundown March 27, 2027. Counting on the biblical calendar (not the modern rabbinic calendar, which puts Passover 2027 in late April), from that day through Yom Kippur, October 7, 2030, gives exactly 1,290 days.

If this reading is right, the trumpet would sound on Yom Teruah, the Feast of Trumpets, in late September 2030. That opens the ten Days of Awe, which close on Yom Kippur, when the 1,290 days end. Jesus said, “but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.” (Matthew 24:22)

WHAT ABOUT “NO MAN KNOWS THE DAY OR HOUR”?

Some will point to Matthew 24:36: “But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.”

That is a fair question, and it deserves a fair answer. Here are both sides, with the verses written out.

The case that the timing will be understood at the end:

Jesus said “knoweth,” which is present tense. When He spoke, no one knew.

Daniel was told the timing was sealed only until a set point: “Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end... none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand.” (Daniel 12:9-10)

Paul told believers they would not be caught off guard: “But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief.” (1 Thessalonians 5:4)

Jesus said the thief comes on those who are not watching: “If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee.” (Revelation 3:3)

I also believe “the day no man knows” may have been a Hebrew expression for the Feast of Trumpets. That feast falls on the new moon, and its exact day could only be confirmed when the new moon was sighted. I offer this as a possibility to study, not as proven fact.

The case for caution:

After His resurrection, Jesus told the disciples: “It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power.” (Acts 1:7)

He also warned: “Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.” (Matthew 24:44)

Many believers read these verses to mean no one should set dates.

Where both sides agree:

We are commanded to watch: “Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.” (Matthew 24:42)

We are expected to recognize the season: “So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.” (Matthew 24:33)

So weigh it for yourself. That is what the Bereans did: “they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” (Acts 17:11)

THE POINT OF THE PAIN

Labor is never the goal. The baby is.

“A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come: but as soon as she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world.” (John 16:21)

“For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.” (Romans 8:22)

If the pains are growing stronger, that is no reason to fear. It is a reason to wake up.

“And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” (Luke 21:28)

“Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.” (Luke 21:36)

Read Matthew 24 this week, and check every reference above. Then ask yourself one question:

If the contractions are getting closer, are you ready for the birth?

text:
If you really want $STRC and other digital credit products to be able to attract hundreds of billions, if not TRILLIONS, of capital through their products in the future, you need it to be a product that can attract that volume of capital.

That wont happen if the company allows it to sit at $90-95 for 6-12 months whist they 'wait' for the market to move it. 

Institutions with hundreds of billions of dollars to invest want security first. The rate of return is secondary.

Most people on X speak as if its the other way around.

Institutions want assurances that if they allocate $50B of capital into $STRC, they'll not only receive their 12% return, but they'll also not wake up one morning & see that their $50B of shares is now only worth $40B & they'll have to 'wait 6 months for the market to push it back up'. 

It's @saylor's and @phongle's job to engineer. construct and manage the product accordingly to ensure that those two things happen. 

Action over passiveness. It's that simple. 

If they can consistently demonstrate that confidence to institutions (over multiple years, not days or months!), the amount of capital they'll be able to attract will continue to grow.

Buybacks offer the best defence to keep it pegged to par.  

It sends a message to the market that getting STRC to par is a priority and they're going to defend it relentlessly. That gives confidence to larger investors that their invested capital is 'safe'.

I see people complaining that Strategy have diluted the common shareholder in recent months and they could have simply increased the rate and waited for it to return to par.

They complain that Strategy have spent $2.6B on STRC buybacks, but don't consider that by doing so and providing confidence to institutions that they are prepared to defend it and keep it close to par, that it could open up the door to 10 institutions all committing to invest $5B to STRC.

Passiveness over action. Hope over action.

The ultimate goal should be to be an issuer at $100.01 and a buyer below $100 and to peg it to par indefinitely.

There's $300T of capital in the fixed income market. I want Strategy to get as much of the capital through STRC over the next decade. 

They wont get there unless they can keep STRC pegged to par. 

Their action this year are laying the foundations for them to build over the next 20-50 years. 

Think ₿igger.

text:
Grok Bot just got an update with v1.2.0! 🚀

Flight redesign and hotel maps

Changelog v1.2.0

New:
• Google phone checks in a Bot's message show a Google verification card with a QR code to scan or open on your phone. Requires Grok Bot 1.1.0 or later.
• Team admins can turn off Proactive messages for the team's Bots from the dashboard. (Teams)
• Connectors that use your organization's single sign-on connect with Sign in with SSO, and your browser returns you to the Bot afterward. (Enterprise)
• Hotel photos open in a full-size viewer with the hotel name, a photo counter, thumbnails, and previous and next buttons.
• Hotel and place maps have Zoom in and Zoom out buttons, the Location map can be dragged and recentered, and hotel pages add Copy address.
• In the expanded Mermaid diagram view, right-click and choose Copy Image to copy the diagram as a PNG.

Improved:
• Flight results are redesigned: select a flight to see Full details and Book, or expand it for bags, changes, and refund rules.
• Flight searches show their steps, such as Searching flights and Checking the fare, and Book buttons hide while the Bot books that flight.
• When no flights match your airline, departure time, or stop filters, the Bot shows the closest options and says which filters it relaxed.
• The Tasks page groups Done, Canceled, and Archived tasks into one Closed section, with filters for each and search.
• On the Tasks page, click a task's files pill to list its files and open any of them, and task tags show as colored pills.
• Follow-ups, corrections, and repeats of tracked work continue the existing task and build on its earlier results instead of starting over.
• When the Bot rewrites a Page you have open, a New updates available pill loads the latest version at your scroll position.
• Clicking Update closes the dialog at once, the sidebar shows checking, download, and preparing progress, and Grok Bot restarts when ready.
• Take over and End call on a live phone call card ask you to confirm first, so a misclick no longer ends or transfers the call.
• Command approval cards show the exact command in full with hidden characters marked, and Allow once runs it one time only.
• Opening a prompt link asks you to confirm before it fills a Bot's chat box, and links with suspicious hidden characters are blocked.
• Open a Bot in its own window with New window in its right-click menu; double-clicking a sidebar row no longer pops it out.
• In Quick Chat, the element you pick stays highlighted in your Bot's color, and on macOS the Bot also sees the page title, address, and highlighted text.
• Product pages show up to four options per group with Show all, and About and Reviews sections with the rating and review count.
• Hotel pages show the review score with stars and the review count, the Website detail opens the hotel's site, and the map lists hotels beside it.
• Hotel and car rental results show the search radius in miles or kilometers to match your computer's settings.
• Shopping cards leave out products without a real photo when others have one, and a card with no photos arrives as a text list.
• Order tracking checks more often as delivery gets closer, up to hourly once a package is out for delivery.
• Before showing an order card, the Bot settles checkout contact details such as the receipt email, so payment doesn't stall after you tap Pay.
• When a sign-in page offers only a QR code to scan, the Bot sends you its link to tap instead.
• Auto-review decides on large and binary file writes on the Bot's computer, so safe ones go through without an approval card.
• The Bot's remote browser starts several seconds faster when it carries over your sign-ins, cookies, and open tabs.
• Automations that control the desktop type and respond much faster, matching interactive computer use.
• In meetings, the Bot picks up your answer to its question, or the rest of your request, said within a minute without its name.
• Asking the Bot to share a Project returns the Project's page and says who can join: the team, invitees only, or only its owner.
• When you're added to a Team Bot, its intro message can mention its role, its owner, and which team accounts it uses. (Teams)
• MCP tools you turn off for a server in your desktop MCP settings are also hidden and refused in your own Grok Bot turns, including routines.
• Flight searches check fares from more sources, so results come back more reliably with comparison options.
• Connector controls read Sign In, Sign In Again, and Sign Out, and apps that run locally say Runs on your computer after you sign in.
• On a team Bot, people who can use but not edit the Bot can click its skills in chat to view them read-only. (Teams)
• Unconnected plugins in the @ menu show just the plugin name and a Connect action.
• HTML file previews run without network access, so remote scripts, stylesheets, fonts, and images no longer load.
• Large Excel workbooks show their first rows right away while the rest of the sheet loads.
• The sidebar resize handle can be focused with Tab and resized with the arrow keys, Home, and End.
• Team admins manage Grok Bot network mode, allowed destinations, and team blocked sites from Security, beside the organization's blocked sites. (Teams)
• Group MCP allowlist imports show whether each rule applies Local only, Cloud only, or Local and Cloud, and ask you to confirm each surface's first rule. (Teams)
• The Setup column for customer-hosted computers shows each computer's team setup script status, with revisions and failure details on hover. (Enterprise)
• Team setup scripts set to run outside the guest container receive the team's Team Secrets and setup files. (Teams)
• When context sync is off, a Project's Notes page and Library say Context sync is not running instead of a generic loading error.

Fixed:
• Chat uploads over 25 MB, including videos, reach the Bot's computer so it can open and work with them.
• The Bot stops computer tasks stuck repeating the same clicks, and a hung click, keystroke, or wait stops after 30 seconds and tries something else.
• Computer use clicks land on their target instead of drifting up and to the left.
• Browser and screenshot tools wake the Bot's sleeping computer instead of refusing.
• Browser and desktop tasks no longer stop with a model not offered in your region error; the Bot switches to an available model.
• Hotel searches show bookable rooms and rates for hotels that previously said their rooms couldn't be shown.
• When a store doesn't accept your card's brand, the Bot offers a new order card with an accepted payment option instead of stopping.
• When X Money card payments aren't enabled for your account, the Bot says so and offers the same order with another payment method.
• Shopping and product cards appear reliably, including when the reply also links a product, and order and shipment cards appear in their task's thread.
• The Bot reliably notices when a checkout declines your card or asks for it again, and uses your own email for receipts and order updates.
• Approving a purchase card while the Bot replaces it no longer shows the new card as expired, and the replaced card shows as expired.
• Card numbers, expiry dates, and security codes are removed from memories, including long ones, team memory, Bots shared as templates, and forget requests held for review.
• Before filling a saved login, the Bot opens the site's sign-in page, and a fill that stalls stops after two minutes.
• When filling a form you answered, the Bot checks the open tab, so a crafted page address can't send your answers to another site.
• Connectors linked through your own account work in your private Grok Bot chats instead of showing as not connected.
• Connected apps no longer disappear for hours after a brief outage, and your MCP tools stay available when the server list briefly can't be read.
• Changes to your team's MCP allowlist and connector settings take effect right away, including after you add, edit, or remove a skill. (Teams)
• On Slack and X Chat, replies about a connector or plugin your team admin blocked name it and say it's disabled by your admin. (Teams)
• When a team admin has turned MCP servers off, the Bot refuses adding one right away instead of showing an approval card first. (Teams)
• Group MCP rules that list no servers keep the team's MCP servers, and Local only or Cloud only rules keep team servers allowed for Grok Bot. (Teams)
• In Slack, a shared Bot's sign-in link for a team-added connector opens a working sign-in page. (Teams)
• Skill links in replies on Slack and Teams show as their plain name instead of raw link text.
• A Grok Bot running on a team's own computer no longer picks up skills from the owner's personal computer. (Teams)
• An email to your Bot's inbox wakes a bot on that inbox's team, never one from another team.
• Grok Bot can read and upload SharePoint files in chats with no team selected.
• Meeting notes no longer get dropped when they take longer than 45 seconds to write.
• Transferring a Grok Bot's ownership completes reliably and pauses the previous owner's routines.
• Routines finish running their code before reporting back, and a routine deleted elsewhere is reported as already deleted.
• Work handed to another of your bots no longer leaves a task stuck in For Review.
• The Bot recovers when its code checker times out or a server hiccups mid-task, instead of ending with the work undone.
• A connector tool with a self-referencing input schema no longer stops the Bot from using your other connector tools.
• Asking for a usage breakdown of more than 20 bots or routines lists the top 20 with a note instead of failing.
• Publishing a skill to your team refuses links and unreadable files in its folder and names the entry to fix. (Teams)
• With a proxy set on the Bot's computer, healthy windows no longer restart, and taking over to sign in brings the open page forward.
• Editing a Page with the Bot keeps its summary, link preview card, live data, and visualizations, and printing or saving it as PDF includes the whole Page.
• The consent page for connecting an outside app to Grok Bot loads reliably for users with many bots.
• Grok Bot no longer says your phone isn't connected when the device status check is slow or the app is briefly in the background.
• The Test Setup Scripts panel in team settings masks Team Secrets and setup file URLs that scripts print. (Teams)
• Clicking Update installs the newest build, including when a newer version is downloading or a restart for an update failed on macOS.
• When a monthly spend limit blocks sends after buying credits, the banner stays visible and offers Increase limit.
• The Messages connector reads chats on macOS 14 and earlier, and older Macs say they need macOS 14 or later.
• The plugins dialog loads plugin status and skills for people on several teams, and plugins your admin disabled hide their Setup section.
• Signing out on desktop switches you to your other saved account instead of showing the sign-in screen.
• Connectors that need a data center before sign-in show a connect card where you pick it, and Connect shows Connecting… until you're signed in.
• Connectors on the From Grok shelf in Connect Apps show their logos and their server's host.
• Read-only tools in the built-in pull request connector count as reads, so Read-only bots can use them.
• Inline MCP App cards fill the conversation width and expand to their full height, so tall widgets are no longer cut off.
• Hotel photos load reliably, and hotel, car rental, and place pages scroll every tile and room card into view and let you select text.
• After a declined or cancelled flight booking, the trip card shows Book again, and expired cheaper fares no longer show a Book for button.
• Clicking a link inside a Page opens it in your browser, even on Pages with draggable strips or carousels.
• Pressing Enter twice quickly on a Search result opens it without sending the draft in the Prompt.
• Closing menus, dialogs, and panels with Escape returns keyboard focus to where you were, and dialogs open with focus on their first field.
• Keyboard shortcuts in a popped-out chat act on that window, and shortcuts no longer change the chat behind an open dialog.
• On Linux, the title bar Minimize, Maximize, and Close buttons work while a dialog that can't be dismissed is open.
• The Thinking indicator stays on a running turn after a reload or relaunch, and shows when a credit grant pays for the reply.
• The Tasks list and the chat header agree on which tasks are working, scrolling fast no longer shows blank rows, and long task titles truncate.
• A Bot profile's Routines section no longer gets stuck on Loading…, and a saved time zone that isn't valid no longer breaks it.
• Webhook routines on shared team Bots explain that only the owner can get the URL and key, or that team settings block personal API keys. (Teams)
• A teammate's new or shared bot no longer flashes in your own bot list in the sidebar and tray. (Teams)
• A skill name after @ in a reply, such as @pack-for-rain, links to the skill, and prompt links no longer fill a message box.
• Searching the Ctrl+K palette for emoji or symbols finds Bots and Pages with them in their names.
• Link preview cards close when you click outside or scroll, and checklists in chat match the spacing of other lists.
• Changing the language keeps Settings open on the same section, and onboarding fits small windows.
• Plugin account names over 255 characters show the limit inline, and the avatar editor no longer errors when the Bot's computer is unreachable.

text:
Imagine thirteen-year-old Harry Potter entering the race for Minister for Magic as a joke, only to wake up and discover that the entire wizarding world has elected him. The idea is hilarious, especially considering what happens in Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban. Harry is still struggling with homework, Quidditch, Dementors, and the supposed threat of Sirius Black. Now imagine him receiving an official letter informing him that he's responsible for the Ministry of Magic. However, there's an important distinction between canon and this hypothetical scenario. Although the Minister for Magic is generally chosen through elections, J.K. Rowling's supplementary Wizarding World writings indicate that elections are ordinarily held at intervals of no more than seven years, with emergency appointments possible. The claim that candidates can enter for twelve Galleons with no minimum age isn't established in the seven novels or the films. But assuming those rules existed, Harry's unexpected victory would create absolute chaos. The Boy Who Lived would suddenly become the Boy Who Governed, and the Ministry would have to explain how a third-year Hogwarts student had become the most powerful political figure in magical Britain.

The funniest part is imagining how the established characters would react and how quickly the joke could turn into a political disaster. Cornelius Fudge, who is Minister during Harry's third year, would probably be furious at losing his position to a thirteen-year-old. Lucius Malfoy and other influential pure-blood families might challenge the result, while Rita Skeeter would have enough material for sensational headlines for months. Hermione would probably end up explaining Ministry regulations to Harry, Ron would be delighted by the absurdity of it all, and Dumbledore would likely recognize how dangerous Harry's sudden political influence could become. Interestingly, Rowling's official history confirms that Dumbledore was repeatedly offered the position of Minister but refused it, showing that even highly respected wizards could be reluctant to accept such power. But imagine the consequences for Voldemort's return. Instead of having to convince a hostile Ministry that Voldemort was back, Harry might actually have the authority to order investigations, strengthen Hogwarts's defenses, and prepare the wizarding community years earlier. Of course, possessing political power at thirteen wouldn't automatically make him capable of using it wisely. And that's what makes this alternate universe so entertaining: Harry could defeat a troll, survive a Basilisk, and face Voldemort, yet still find himself completely unprepared for the most terrifying challenge of all running the British Ministry of Magic while trying to finish his Potions homework.

text:
What if a church bore the name of life and yet stood dead before the Lord?

Sardis holds a living name while its works fade, and Laodicea boasts of wealth while it stays poor, blind, and naked.

The Lord knocks and waits to come in, promising white garments and a name kept in the book of life.

Discover the challenge and the invitation in Revelation 3:1-6, 14-22.

The Door and the Knock

Many Catholics can still hear an older English line about this scene. Christ stands at the door and knocks. In the New Revised Standard Version Catholic Edition, Revelation 3 gives that moment a clear and tender voice: "I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me." The words sit inside a hard letter to two churches that look fine from the street. Sardis has a name of being alive, but it is dead. Laodicea is neither cold nor hot. The image matters because it refuses both panic and pride. The Lord of the churches does not kick the door down. He waits. He speaks. He asks for an answer.

A Love That Will Not Force the Lock

The knock belongs to a love that tells the truth. Earlier in the same reading, Christ says, "I reprove and discipline those whom I love." That line keeps the knock from turning soft or vague. Laodicea boasts, "I am rich, I have prospered, and I need nothing," and does not see that it is wretched, pitiable, poor, blind, and naked. Sardis must wake up and strengthen what remains, because a good reputation cannot hide a thin faith. The door in this passage is not a prop in a painting only. It is the daily threshold of a parish, a household, and a heart that has grown used to spiritual noise. Christ offers gold refined by fire, white robes, and salve for the eyes. Those gifts correct the lie that comfort equals holiness. The knock is judgment and mercy in one sound. Judgment, because lukewarm self-trust cannot host God. Mercy, because the one who conquers is promised a name kept in the book of life and a place with Christ on his throne.

The Meal on the Other Side

What waits past the door is not a lecture. It is a meal. The same verse promises, "I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me." In Catholic life, that promise reaches toward the altar, where Christ gives himself as food. It also reaches toward the ordinary table, where faith becomes hospitality. Eating with someone means staying, sharing, and being known. The verse ties that intimacy to a condition that is simple and costly. A person must hear his voice and open the door. Opening can look like confession after a long absence. It can look like a return to Sunday Mass. It can look like honest prayer, or like a choice to stop managing an image and tell God the truth. White clothes in the letter to Sardis point to a life made clean enough to walk with Christ. The knock does not expire because a soul feels late, dull, or ashamed. It continues as long as love continues. The reading leaves the choice with the one who hears. The door opens from within, when love is answered with a yes.

THE GREAT DECEPTION — PEACE, PROSPERITY & THE CHAINS YOU CANNOT SEE!
Daniel 11:24 describes a ruler who enters prosperous places peacefully and distributes plunder and riches. While historically associated with Antiochus IV, some Christians also see a foreshadowing of the Antichrist.
Imagine a world offering everything you’ve ever wanted!
Money, food, entertainment, pleasure, peace, and security. Everyone comfortable, distracted, and satisfied.
BUT LOOK CLOSER—THEY’RE CHAINED TO THE VERY THINGS THEY BELIEVE HAVE SET THEM FREE!
Daniel 8:25 warns, “And by peace shall destroy many.”
1 Thessalonians 5:3 warns, “For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them.”
In the futurist interpretation of Daniel 9:27, a final seven-year period is divided at the three-and-a-half-year mark. Many understand this as a covenant associated with the Antichrist, followed by intensified deception and persecution. Scripture does not promise that everyone will enjoy peace or prosperity during the first half.
THEN THE MASK COMES OFF!
What appeared to be freedom becomes bondage. What appeared to be provision becomes control. The comforts people trusted become the very things used to enslave them!
Revelation 13:16–17 warns that buying and selling will be restricted to those bearing the mark of the beast.
Revelation 20:4 describes those beheaded for their testimony of Jesus Christ and their refusal to worship the beast or receive his mark.
THE WORLD OFFERED THEM EVERYTHING—EXCEPT ETERNAL LIFE!
They were entertained into complacency, comforted into dependence, and deceived into believing they were free.
THE CHAINS WERE THERE ALL ALONG!
Jesus warned in Matthew 24:4, “Take heed that no man deceive you.”
The exact prophetic timeline is interpreted differently among Christians, but the warning is unmistakable: Do not trade eternal truth for temporary comforts!
WAKE UP! WATCH! BE READY!
Peace without Christ cannot save you. Riches cannot redeem you. And the world cannot give you what only Jesus Christ can offer—ETERNAL LIFE!
CHOOSE JESUS NOW, WHILE THE DOOR IS OPEN!

text:
In Japan, when a child starts first grade, the grandparents buy the backpack.

It's called a randoseru. It is not a backpack the way you're thinking. It's a hard leather box with straps. It costs about as much as a used motor scooter. It has to survive six years of a Japanese child. First graders wearing them look like very small, very determined turtles.

Grandparents start shopping a year early. There's even a name for it. Ran-katsu. "Backpack hunting." It is taken extremely seriously.

My coworker, Mr. Kurimoto, is 66. His grandson, Kai, started first grade this April. Mr. Kurimoto began his ran-katsu eleven months before that. He built a spreadsheet. Forty-three models. Ranked by stitching.

His daughter is married to a Texan named Tate.

And Tate's father is Garland. Seventy-nine. San Angelo, Texas. He has made saddles by hand in the same shop for fifty-five years.

Last summer, Garland heard about the backpack.

He called his son. "Now hold on. It's leather? It's handmade? It has to carry a boy for six years?"

"Yes, Dad."

"Son. That's a saddle."

Then Tate told him the price.

"For a backpack? I've sold saddles for less. And those carry a grown man."

So now there were two grandfathers. One backpack. And a problem.

Nobody in our office is more polite than Mr. Kurimoto. He offered, through his daughter, to step aside.

Garland said, "No sir. We do it together."

What followed was four months of two old men, 7,000 miles apart, building one backpack through a translation app.

Mr. Kurimoto sent fourteen pages of specifications. Exact measurements. School regulations. A diagram of the inside of a Japanese first grader's day.

Garland's reply to the fourteen pages was one line.

"WILL HOLD BOY. — G."

Then he sent back a photo after every step.

Mr. Kurimoto replied to every photo in red.

"Stitching: excellent."
"Rivet three: concerned."
"Strap: please consider the shoulders of a six-year-old."

Garland replied, "Yes sir." Every single time. He has not said "yes sir" to anyone that many times since basic training in 1965.

It arrived in Tokyo in March. Dark brown leather. Oak leaves tooled into the flap by hand. Kai's name stamped in English on one side and in Japanese on the other. Garland had Tate send him the Japanese characters. He practiced them on scrap leather for seven days. And on the bottom, where only the floor would ever see it, a small Texas star. Next to it, a cherry blossom. He had asked Mr. Kurimoto to draw him one.

When school started, Kai's whole class lined up to smell it.

"It smells like a horse," one boy said.

"It smells like America," said another.

The teacher inspected it, smelled it, and said, "Approved."

Then, two weeks ago, a strap needed adjusting, and Kai's mother lifted the lining inside the lid.

There was a hidden pocket.

Inside it was an envelope. Garland's handwriting.

"For Kai. Open at your sixth-grade graduation. March 2032. — Grandpa."

She hadn't known about it. Nobody had.

Then she found the second envelope.

Same pocket. Behind the first one. Japanese handwriting. Her father's.

"For Kai. Open at your sixth-grade graduation. March 2032. — Jiji."

Neither grandfather knew the other one had done it. Garland had built the pocket. Mr. Kurimoto had found it on the first night, when he inspected every seam with a flashlight, and quietly added his own.

And each envelope had one more line, on the back.

On Garland's, in pencil:

"If I ain't there, have Mr. Kurimoto read it to him. He'll do it right."

On Mr. Kurimoto's, in careful English, letter by letter:

"If I cannot attend, please ask Mr. Garland to read mine also."

Two old men. Two countries. Same pocket. Same date. Each one had picked the other as his backup.

Kai's mother put both envelopes back exactly where she found them, closed the lining, and told no one but her husband. And me, because I asked why Mr. Kurimoto came into the office last week walking ten thousand steps a day.

Garland has a bad heart. Mr. Kurimoto has a bad knee. Both of them did the math. March 2032.

Garland has quit smoking. His doctor has never had a patient quit for a backpack. Mr. Kurimoto has quit taking the elevator. Our office is on the ninth floor. He arrives every morning breathing like a typhoon, and very proud.

Two grandfathers, half a planet apart, are now in a quiet competition to stay alive long enough to watch a boy open their letters.

Kai doesn't know any of this. He's six. He just knows his backpack smells like a horse, and that both of his grandfathers ask him every single day if it's holding up.

It's holding up.

So are they.

text:
The Twelve Months Sanctified by Prayer: November, Month of the Souls in Purgatory by M. L'ABBE A. RICARD, D.S.G. Translated from the French. 1877 November 22 FASTING.
.
Prelude.
.
Let us represent to ourselves the fearful austerities which are practised by so many religious orders, both men and women. throughout the whole Church. From them spring a treasure of merit in which the merciful justice of God is pleased to make the souls in Purgatory participate.
.
Meditation.
.
We read in the First Book of Kings that, "when the inhabitants of Jabes Galaad bad heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul, all the most valiant men arose and walked all the night, and took the body of Saul, and the bodies of his sons, from the wall of Bethsan: and they came to Jabes Galaad, and burnt them there; and they took their bones. and buried them in the wood of Jabes, and fasted seven days."
.
This example shows us how for ages the faithful have fasted for the dead, and we see with lively admiration that this practice has at all times been approved and followed in the, Catholic Church. Besides, under the name of­ fasts all other mortifications and austerities are comprehended, as disciplines, hair-cloth, lying on the ground, etc.
O my Jesus, Thou Who hast said that, "As long as you did it to one of these My least brethren, you did it to Me," what pretext then in my cowardice find to dispense me from helping the souls in Purgatory, knowing that the good which I should do them would not be less agreeable to Thee, than if I had done it to, Thyself? I offer Thee then for them all the· mortifications which I resolve to practice for their intention.
.
Resolution.
.
Shake off our cowardice, so as to embrace courageously the practices of voluntary penance, in favour of the poor souls in Purgatory.
.
Aspiration.
.
And they took their bones and buried them in the wood of Jabes, and fasted seven days." (1 Kings xxxi. 13.)
.
EXAMPLE: CONTINUAL PRESENCE OF A SOUL.
.
We read the following incident in the annals of the Visitation of Dijon: Sister Mary Bernard Chicolier, who attained to great sanctity, was prevented by special, graces from her earliest years. She formed, when quite young, the design of consecrating herself to God, and was clothed, and made her profession under the government of our mother, Anne Lidwine Boulier. The Mere Chahu, who was her successor, helped this dear sister, amidst the great trials through which it pleased God to make her pass, and Who imprinted in her heart a most lively horror of the smallest imperfections by permitting a soul in Purgatory to appear to her, and to be in a manner continually present to her. Our mother, to whom this dear sister disclosed all that she suffered, caused her to be examined by M. Chaudot, our superior, and by the Rev. Father Jacquinot) Provincial of the Society of Jesus, who after a serious examination, judged that there was in this neither illu­sion nor imagination. It was, therefore, decided that the community should have masses celebrated, and recite every day a De profundis for the repose of this soul, and that Sister Chicolier should be at liberty to make particular penances for this intention. This dear sister practiced great austerities, offering besides for this soul, all her good works, which were very numerous, and never allowing herself a single inclination of nature, or the slightest satisfaction. The priest, who was charged with celebrating the Masses, was a Capuchin monk of great holiness, and who entirely ignored everything that had happened. He came one day to find Mere Chahu, and assured her that the soul whom she had caused to be prayed so much for, had entered into possession of the glory of God.

text:
No, California's new law is not an automatic ban on creatine for anyone under 18. Creatine is one factor a court "may consider." The real test is whether a product is labeled, marketed or sold for weight loss or muscle building, and creatine sold that way is covered.

Ace's Report Card: Dietary supplements for weight loss and OTC diet pills; under-18 sales (CA AB 2030, Ch. 720/2026) (signed Sept 28, 2026; effective Jan 1, 2027)

The Deal: No one may sell, offer to sell, or give away as a promotion covered weight-loss or muscle-building supplements or OTC diet pills to anyone under 18. Penalties are civil, up to $500 per violation, enforced by the AG, county counsel or city attorneys, with attorney's fees for a prevailing plaintiff. There is a prescription exception.

Poker Hand: The house raises the age limit on one aisle. The label, not just the ingredient list, decides which products are in that aisle.

Title Integrity: A. The title matches the Health and Safety Code chapter. Receipt: Ch. 720 title; 109030.
Transparency: C. "Labeled, marketed, or otherwise represented" turns on multi-factor court findings, and the in-store ID trigger wording is awkward. Receipt: 109030(b)(2), (e).
Fiscal: C (judgment, unscored). No official fiscal note with dollar figures retrieved; the digest marks Fiscal Committee: Yes / Appropriation: No. Receipt: Legislative Counsel's Digest.
Liberty: C. Age-gates a class of lawful adult products statewide, including how stores tag and group them. Receipt: 109030(b), (e)(4).
Ideological Capture: B. Open and germane. A bill requiring those sales to minors by the same mechanism would get the same grade. Receipt: 109030.
Special Interests: B. It burdens sellers of covered products broadly; industry groups led by the Council for Responsible Nutrition opposed it. Cal-Access-based totals for Josh Lowenthal for Assembly 2026 (ID 1477066): about $966K contributions and about $893K expenditures through Sept. 30, 2026 (TransparencyUSA reading of SOS filings); top contributors include SEIU-linked and trades PACs. No supplement-industry earmark tied to AB 2030 found. Receipt: CRN retailer FAQ; Cal-Access/TransparencyUSA committee page.
Enforceability: C. Civil-only, but coverage depends on marketing factors courts "may consider," including creatine content and store placement. Receipt: 109030(e), (d).

Hidden Gotchas
- Creatine, green tea extract, raspberry ketone, garcinia cambogia, and green coffee bean extract are coverage factors, not an automatic ban. Labeling, implied claims, and how the retailer groups the product also count. (Confidence: High) 109030(e)(1)-(4).
- The in-store ID rule says request ID if the retailer "cannot reasonably determine that the person appears to be under 18." Retailer guidance restates that as checking when the buyer does not clearly appear at least 18. Courts will have to sort the wording. (Confidence: Medium) 109030(b)(2); CRN Need-to-Know.
- Online sellers must use a government-source age database, an adult photo-ID signature on delivery, or both. Under-18s with a prescription are exempt. (Confidence: High) 109030(c), (f).

The River Card: Backers point to eating-disorder and youth-supplement risks. Opponents, including the Council for Responsible Nutrition, say the law chills truthful claims and will confuse store clerks. Gov. Newsom signed it with other health bills on Sept 28. It takes effect Jan 1, 2027.

Ace's Call: Call. Clarify the in-store ID trigger in a cleanup bill, and say plainly in guidance that creatine alone does not ban a product.

Confidence: High on the chaptered text; Medium on how courts will read the ID clause.

Journalist Angle Note: Viral posts treat creatine as the ban; the statute lists it as one of several factors a court may weigh.

Sources Used: California Leginfo (chaptered text, digest); CRN retailer FAQ; Governor's Sept 28 signing release.

LMAO. 😂 Well, your Xbox-branded profile certainly explains a lot!

But since you want to talk TECHNICAL SPECS, let's correct a few things!

"PS5 doesn't even have RDNA 2."

FALSE! Sony's official PS5 specifications explicitly state AMD Radeon RDNA 2-based graphics architecture.

Both PS5 and Xbox Series X launched in 2020 using AMD Zen 2 CPUs and RDNA 2-based GPUs!

Series X has more raw GPU compute power than the BASE PS5 on paper. Congratulations!

But PS5 Pro offers a substantially upgraded GPU, advanced ray tracing, and PSSR upscaling.

Finding a few games where Xbox performs better doesn't establish that its hardware is universally superior. Performance varies by game and optimization!

"Xbox has the same third-party support."

There's significant overlap, absolutely!

But that doesn't mean identical libraries!

PlayStation also has games like Astro Bot, Gran Turismo 7, Demon's Souls, Ghost of Yōtei, and SAROS that aren't available on Xbox.

And Microsoft is increasingly bringing its OWN franchises to PlayStation!

Forza Horizon, Gears of War, Sea of Thieves, Indiana Jones, Microsoft Flight Simulator, and more!

"Most PlayStation exclusives are single-player."

And that's a BAD thing?!

God of War, Spider-Man, Horizon, and The Last of Us are celebrated largely for their single-player experiences!

Xbox has single-player games too, genius!

And apparently you've forgotten Gran Turismo 7, Helldivers 2, Destiny 2, and PlayStation's enormous selection of multiplayer games.

"Xbox has customizable controllers."

And PlayStation has DualSense Edge!

Remappable buttons, adjustable triggers, back buttons, custom profiles, and a headphone jack!

PLUS adaptive triggers, advanced haptics, motion controls, and a built-in speaker!

"Xbox has Meta Quest."

You mean streaming conventional Xbox games onto a virtual screen inside a headset?

That's NOT the same as PSVR2 running actual immersive VR games with eye tracking, tracked controllers, and VR gameplay!

"Xbox has better backward compatibility."

Now THAT'S a legitimate advantage!

Xbox supports selected original Xbox and Xbox 360 games, plus Xbox One titles.

Meanwhile, PS5 supports the overwhelming majority of more than 4,000 PS4 games!

Both have strengths. See how easy it is to acknowledge facts?

"Xbox has a better ecosystem."

That's your OPINION!

Xbox emphasizes Game Pass, PC integration, and cloud gaming.

PlayStation emphasizes an enormous console library, DualSense, PSVR2, PlayStation Plus, Remote Play, physical gaming options, and powerful hardware.

And Sony has surpassed 100 MILLION PS5s shipped!

Apparently millions of consumers see value in something you insist offers practically nothing.

I never said Xbox had NO advantages.

YOU claimed PlayStation offered very little, then proceeded to list features Xbox ALSO has while getting Sony's actual hardware specifications wrong!

And the funniest part?

You accuse PlayStation owners of brand loyalty while displaying Xbox branding on your own profile!

Liking Xbox doesn't make PlayStation's advantages disappear.

Maybe compare the platforms objectively instead of confusing your personal preferences with technical facts!

text:
Under either Sanders or Jayapal's proposal, HHS sets a national budget and the government decides which treatments qualify for coverage. So, a hospital that wants to expand care needs for the govt to fund it. There is a difference between making medical decisions, which is protected for doctors, and allocating money for health care, which is not. Doctors could not necessarily expand the number of patients their institution could see. Govt will also ration health care indirectly by setting reimbursement rates. 

Canada has a system close to this and currently guidance is offered on managing volume of patients and which patients to prioritize. Taiwan appears to have a similar system to Medicare for All and do better, but the US as a whole is politically and culturally more similar to Canada. You mentioned seeing a doctor for a cold in the US but it's PCPs that generally have longer wait times in America and specialists with shorter wait times, right? 

When (not if) funding doesn't match demand, hospitals will cut staff, postpone procedures, or take fewer appointments. Congress and the president will face pressure to revise eligibility and set stricter government guidelines. It might be doctors doing the rationing on paper but operating on the basis of economic incentives shaped by the government.

text:
What is @Rivian afraid of & can you imagine a vendor offers you a solution to drive you competing with @Tesla and says you can’t describe it you can’t take pictures you can’t talk about it and you can’t video it? WTH! 

Rivian is actively rolling out its next major autonomy feature: Point-to-Point supervised driving.
Current status (as of mid-November 2026)
Rivian has begun inviting selected owners into its Autonomy Early Access Program to test Point-to-Point.
•It is a supervised, hands-free system (driver must still monitor and be ready to take over).
•Drivers enter an address and the vehicle handles the full route: city streets, stop lights, intersections, highway merges/interchanges, etc. — similar to Tesla’s FSD Supervised.
•Eligible vehicles: Gen 2 R1 (R1T/R1S) and R2 with a paid Autonomy+ subscription.
•Starting in California and Florida; other states later.
•Participants must sign a strict agreement that bans publicly posting, filming, or describing the feature. Rivian can retain camera footage for up to five years after they leave the program.
Limited rollout is happening now (late November / December 2026 via over-the-air update to selected owners). A broader release to all Autonomy+ subscribers is targeted for 2027.
Roadmap
Milestone
Target
Notes
Point-to-Point (supervised)
Late 2026 (limited) → 2027 (broader)

Uber robotaxis
Late 2028
Up to 10,000–50,000 R2s under the Uber deal
CEO RJ Scaringe has described Point-to-Point as the first major step toward Level 4 autonomy and said 2027 should be an “inflection year” for Rivian as R2 volume and autonomy scale.
Hardware & software notes
•Current vehicles use cameras + radar.
•Gen 3 autonomy platform (custom RAP1 chip + front-facing long-range LiDAR) is planned to start going into employee vehicles later this year, then customers in 2027. Rivian argues the multi-sensor approach (cameras + radar + LiDAR) will handle weather and edge cases better than camera-only systems.
•Autonomy+ (already available) includes Universal Hands-Free on ~3.5 million miles of roads where lane lines are clear.
Upcoming event
Rivian is hosting its second Autonomy & AI Day on December 9, 2026 in Palo Alto. Expect demos, more details on the roadmap, and possibly early looks at the new hardware/software.
Bottom line: Rivian is moving from expanded hands-free highway driving into full route-to-route supervised autonomy right now, with a controlled Early Access phase underway and broader availability next year. It is explicitly positioning itself as a Tesla FSD competitor, with ambitions for unsupervised and robotaxi use later this decade.

text:
Many Irish people who backed the fuel protests feel let down by the leaders who pulled back and backed down just when the chance for real impact arrived.
For many, its back to the drawing board.

In April, farmers, hauliers, contractors and ordinary drivers brought parts of the country to a near standstill with convoys and blockades over sky-high fuel costs. 
The pressure forced the government into a €505 million package of supports, including cuts to excise. It showed what organised, disruptive action could achieve.

This month offered another clear window. 
Ireland was hosting the European Political Community summit on 12 November, with around 50 world leaders in Dublin, followed by an informal EU leaders’ meeting the next day. 
Security was the biggest the state had ever mounted. 
Roads were restricted, gardaí were out in force, and the eyes of Europe were on the capital. 
A well-timed nationwide rolling protest or convoy could have created maximum visibility and pressure at a moment when the government least wanted disruption.

Instead, organisers with the People of Ireland Against Fuel Prices Protest called off the nationwide element. 

In a social media statement they pointed to garda warnings of a “zero-tolerance” approach to road blockages and any traffic disruption, saying they were not prepared to risk people’s licences, jobs and livelihoods. They also said momentum had been lost, the necessary support simply wasn’t there, and the appetite for another big nationwide action had faded since the Budget. 

A small Dublin protest still went ahead on the Friday, but reports put the turnout at around 45–50 people.

Those who turned up said they had expected thousands and were disappointed by the numbers and the last-minute confusion.

For many who had taken part in April or who are still struggling with fuel prices, the decision looked like backing down in the face of the state. 
The EPC timing was widely seen as the best opportunity in months to force the issue again while the government was under international scrutiny. 
Calling it off, combined with the tiny Dublin turnout and the admission that support had drained away, has left a bitter taste. 
Some of the more prominent faces from the April protests were not involved this time, and the main haulage association distanced itself. The movement has looked fragmented.

People who felt the April actions delivered results now say the same energy and willingness to confront the authorities was missing when it mattered most. 
The problems they protested about expensive diesel and petrol, pressure on farms, haulage firms and ordinary households have not gone away. 
Yet the leaders who organised the biggest previous actions are viewed by a growing number as having stepped back rather than pressing forward. 

As a result, many have lost confidence in those figures and groups and are looking for other voices or ways to push the same concerns. 

The sense among a sizeable section of those affected is that a rare chance for maximum impact was missed, and trust has been damaged.

text:
🚨 The Stormont Brake Was Always a Paper Shield 🚨

I’ve just heard that the Secretary of State has refused to pull the Stormont Brake on the EU’s new Union Customs Code. The Ulster Unionists are calling the so-called democratic safeguards in the Windsor Framework worthless. They’re right.

This is exactly what many of us said would happen. The Brake was presented as the big protection, the mechanism that would allow Northern Ireland’s elected representatives to stop damaging EU rules from being imposed on us. Unionist MLAs triggered it because the new Customs Code deepens the divide within the United Kingdom and strengthens the Irish Sea border. Extra checks, extra costs, more red tape for businesses that just want to trade with the rest of their own country.

And what happens? The Secretary of State simply says no.

That is not a safeguard. That is a gesture. A political comfort blanket designed to get the Framework over the line, not to give this place any real control. When the moment comes to use it, the decision still sits in London, and London has decided that divergence inside the United Kingdom is an acceptable price.

I have watched businesses deal with the daily reality of the Protocol and the Framework. The paperwork, the uncertainty, the sense that we are being treated as a special case that is somehow less fully part of the UK internal market. Now we are told that even the emergency brake does not work when unionists try to pull it.

The Prime Minister talks about closer alignment with the EU. Meanwhile his government is prepared to accept more separation between Northern Ireland and Great Britain. That is the real direction of travel, and today’s decision confirms it.

You cannot keep telling people that their place in the United Kingdom is secure while every practical measure makes trading with the rest of the UK harder. You cannot sell a democratic safeguard and then refuse to let it function when the elected representatives of this place try to use it.

The Stormont Brake has been tested and found wanting. That should surprise no one who has watched how these arrangements have operated from the start. The gap between the promises and the reality keeps getting wider.

Unionism needs to stop pretending these mechanisms offer meaningful protection. They do not. The Irish Sea border is being reinforced, not removed. And every refusal to act on the Brake only makes that clearer.

#WindsorFramework #StormontBrake #IrishSeaBorder #UUP #NorthernIreland #Unionism #PUL

1. Kyle Connor (+140)
Ottawa Senators @ Winnipeg Jets

✅ Excellent shooting ability and finishing.
✅ Has the offensive role to generate quality scoring chances.
⚠️ Ottawa can make scoring difficult with structured defensive play.
Verdict: Strong selection. One of my favorite legs.
2. Leon Draisaitl (+125)
Edmonton Oilers @ Florida Panthers
✅ Elite offensive finisher.
✅ Strong power-play scoring threat.
✅ Can score from close range and distance.
⚠️ Florida's defensive structure can limit high-quality opportunities.
Verdict: Very good selection. One of the strongest legs.
3. Nikita Kucherov (+155)
Washington Capitals @ Tampa Bay Lightning
✅ Elite offensive talent.
✅ Excellent shooting and playmaking ability.
✅ Tampa Bay's offensive system creates scoring opportunities.
⚠️ His playmaking tendencies can sometimes result in assists rather than goals.
Verdict: Good selection. I like this price.
4. Beckett Sennecke (+180)
Anaheim Ducks @ St. Louis Blues
✅ Has offensive upside.
✅ +180 offers reasonable value.
⚠️ Less established as a consistent goalscorer than the other selections.
⚠️ St. Louis can be a difficult opponent defensively.
Verdict: Risky. This is one of the first legs I'd reconsider.
5. Steven Stamkos (+200)
Nashville Predators @ Minnesota Wild
✅ Experienced natural goalscorer.
✅ Dangerous on the power play.
✅ +200 provides attractive potential value.
⚠️ His scoring opportunities depend heavily on offensive involvement.
⚠️ Minnesota can limit quality scoring chances.
Verdict: Decent selection, but not a safe goalscorer pick.

text:
Every time you drive past an "Estate Sale" sign, you're driving past an unlisted house you could buy for 30% off

The house was just inherited, there's usually $0 mortgage left, and the kids want a fast check instead of 4 months of repairs

Heres how I use a free website to find these houses 14 days early and buy it for $60k+ off while neighbors fight over $2 coffee mugs:

1. Go to estatesales. net two weeks before the signs go up.

Estate liquidators post upcoming sales 10 to 14 days in advance with 80 to 150 photos of every room, basement corner, and garage

Look past the furniture at the bones of the house.

You get a free inspection from your couch showing the 1970s kitchen, old carpet, electrical panel, and roof overhangs two weeks before a realtor ever touches the property

2. Run the address on your free county auditor site the night before the sale opens, as soon as estatesales. net releases the street address

You want to see two things: that the house hasn't sold in 25+ years (meaning there is $0 mortgage left), and that the tax mailing address for the heirs is in another state.

A son or daughter who flew in from California or Texas for the weekend has a return flight booked for Monday morning and zero desire to manage local contractors for 90 days

3. Skip the Friday morning rush and walk in Sunday at 3:30pm, 30 minutes before the sale ends

By Sunday afternoon the kids are exhausted and staring at 3 bedrooms of heavy 1980s couches, mattresses, and basement junk that didn't sell. Walk up to the family member (or the liquidator running the cash table) and say:

"If you haven't signed with a realtor yet, I buy houses in the neighborhood. Leave every piece of unsold furniture and trash right where it is, skip the 6% realtor commission, and I'll close in 10 days"

(If a liquidation company is running the sale, they love this even more than the family does, because normally the liquidator has to pay a crew $1,500 on Monday to haul the unsold junk to the dump)

Last fall I walked into a 3 bedroom brick ranch outside Columbus at 3:45pm on a Sunday where the daughter had flown in from Arizona to clear out her late dad's house

Clean houses on that street were selling for $215,000, but hers had 1978 green carpet, a 22 yr old roof that wouldn't pass an FHA bank inspection, and two rooms still packed with old encyclopedias and dressers

She took my offer at $142,000 that evening, left the keys on the counter on Monday morning, and flew home

We spent $2,100 emptying the house and $16,500 on a new roof, paint, and vinyl plank floors. Four weeks later the bank appraised it at $218,000, locking in $57,400 of net equity from one Sunday afternoon conversation

She only took $142,000 because I didn't need 45 days and a bank appraiser's permission to close on a house with a 22 yr old roof

We keep $100,000 to $250,000 in 0% introductory business credit sitting under our LLC before we go house hunting

That credit is what lets us close on an inherited fixer upper in days

The entire $18,600 cleanout and renovation sat on that credit at 0% for 12 to 18 months, with nothing reporting to our personal credit score

Once the house was finished, we refinanced into a long-term rental loan and paid that balance off

Most investors and business owners with a 700+ credit score apply for business funding on their own, put "Real Estate" on the application, and get capped at a single $10,000 card, because banks auto-flag real estate as high risk

Unlocking $100,000 to $250,000 at 0% in one round depends on how your LLC is structured for underwriters and how your applications are sequenced across Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion so the hard pulls don't conflict

If you’re a real estate investor or business owner with a 700+ credit score, book a call at the link in my bio and my team will build that $100k to $250k in 0% business credit for you, so you can close on the next inherited fixer-upper in days

authorBio: There’s always more to the story, and the work to “Keep the Republic” has no quitting time.

text:
A New Orleans mayor once gave a house to an emperor who was a whole ocean away, and the house still stands on the corner. 👑

It sits at Chartres and St. Louis streets in the French Quarter, three storeys of old stucco with iron balconies and a small glass cupola on the roof. Today people know it as the Napoleon House. Long before it had that name, it belonged to Nicolas Girod, who served as mayor of New Orleans in the years around the Battle of New Orleans, from 1812 to 1815.

Napoleon Bonaparte was the man who sold Louisiana to the United States in 1803. After his fall, the British sent him to the island of St. Helena in the South Atlantic, a lonely rock in the middle of nowhere. According to the old story, Girod admired the exiled emperor and offered him this house as a refuge, if only he could be freed. 🌍

The story goes further. Some say a group of New Orleans men, including pirates who had fought beside Andrew Jackson, plotted to rescue Napoleon from his island and bring him up the river. The little cupola on the roof, the tale says, was meant to be a lookout where the emperor could watch the ships arrive.

Historians do not agree on how much of this is true. There is no firm proof that the escape plan was ever more than talk. What we do know is that Napoleon never left St. Helena. He died there in 1821, and the house in New Orleans waited for a guest who never came. 🕯️

Still, the legend stuck, and so did the name. The building has been a home, a shop and a restaurant, and its walls have heard two centuries of stories. Locals climb the old stairs. Visitors point at the cupola and ask about the emperor.

That is one of the great things about Louisiana. A house can carry a rumor for two hundred years, and the rumor becomes part of the house.

Next time you walk past a corner building in the Quarter, look up. You might see a lookout that was built for a man who never arrived. ⚜️

From Louisiana Unbound

•  This is a privately funded school (tuition and donations, including a $3.2 million AICP fundraising drive for the campus and co-located Islamic center), not a taxpayer-supported public or charter school; recent Supreme Court rulings such as Carson v. Makin (2022) and Espinoza v. Montana (2020) protect religious private schools from exclusion based on faith when states regulate or offer generally available benefits, making a successful challenge to this routine academic approval unlikely to reach or succeed at the Court.
•  AICP is a longstanding U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit with multiple American campuses and international affiliates; while calls for curriculum and funding transparency are common for any private religious school (and zoning/building approvals remain separate local processes), treating the religious character itself as an improper “cover” would invert the Free Exercise protections that apply equally to Christian, Jewish, or other faith-based private academies already operating under the same rules.

text:
5 REASONS WHY #RAMAYANA PART 1 #FAILED TO EXCITE INDIAN AND GLOBAL AUDIENCES

Lessons for Part 2 — and for the makers of future Mahabharata adaptations

Now that the box office free fall has started, one can safely say Ramayana Part 1 will never recover the claimed budget, given 50-55% of revenues get taken away by exhibitors. Here are the 5 reasons why it failed:

1. You cannot make the villain look like he belongs to a 2026 high-tech fantasy universe and the hero look like he belongs to the early days of filmmaking in 1926.

Audiences have just watched The #Odyssey. There is a similar bow-lifting sequence in it, and it is an absolute edge-of-the-seat spectacle. In Ramayana, the equivalent moment looks almost sissy. If Ravana is being presented at the level of #Thanos, Rama needs to be presented at the level of Odysseus. You cannot have a technologically advanced villain and a visually outdated hero.

2. You cannot have the villain speaking in today’s language, with today’s pace and attitude, while the hero sounds as if he has stepped out of a century-old theatrical production.

The contrast in dialogue, delivery and body language is jarring. What was #Rama doing walking around gardens with Sita and speaking like a pansy? The hero needs to command the same screen presence, linguistic confidence and contemporary cinematic energy as the villain. Grandeur cannot be reserved for the antagonist.

3. You have to practically rule out the older generation from your box-office calculations.

You cannot make Ramayana and #Mahabharata primarily for an older generation that has already watched these epics on television. They remain deeply fascinated by those versions, and all the CGI in the world cannot necessarily change their expectations. The reception from this audience has therefore been understandably cold.

4. Rule Gen Alpha and GenZ out as well! Today’s youth have seen enough Spider-Man, Superman, Thor and The Lord of the Rings to be impressed with yet another fantasy spectacle— that too a mythological. 

They need compelling characters, not just larger-than-life imagery and familiar names. #Ravana was established as a powerful, fascinating character. Rama and Lakshmana, however, were not established with the same cinematic conviction. The audience needs to feel the hero’s power, charisma and extraordinary abilities rather than simply being told about them.

5. So such films will find a market only with those who aren’t elderly and aren’t young. But even the remaining ones aren’t insane. They aren’t excited about Part 2 at all and Part 2 could actually be an even bigger disaster if the makers repeat the same mistakes.

The idea of establishing an army of monkeys led by Hanuman and expecting people to flock to cinemas is a risky proposition. A monkey-man can certainly work, but he needs to look more like a man and less like a monkey. Going by Hanuman’s entry at the end of Part 1, and what the makers did with #Jatayu, there is little indication that they are willing to take the necessary creative risks. Trying to convince today’s generation that a realistic-looking bird can speak is almost as difficult as expecting them to accept ten literal heads on Ravana.

The larger lesson: You cannot simply take an epic that has been told for thousands of years, add expensive CGI, and expect a global cinematic phenomenon. You have to understand the cinematic language, visual expectations and imagination of today’s audience. 

Global audiences loved #RRR but stayed away from Ramayana because the story was put together mindlessly.

The same lessons will apply even more to anyone attempting to make the Mahabharata. Its scale, characters and conflicts offer extraordinary cinematic possibilities. But reverence for the source material cannot become an excuse for unimaginative filmmaking.

text:
How One Citizen Out-Designed a State Election System, For Free 🗳️🗺️

Running an election across Alaska, one-fifth of the U.S. landmass, is a massive logistical challenge, yet the biggest hurdle for voters isn't the physical distance; it's broken digital infrastructure. While official Division of Elections tools force Alaskans to bounce between dense PDFs, dead links, and crashing portals, independent developer Phil Izon built https://t.co/ovf15IJ4i9 Election Map using open government GIS data to fix the experience:

Two-Click Simplicity: Type in an address or drop a pin to instantly see your legislative district, turn-by-turn directions to your polling place, and self-hosted sample ballots that stay online even when state servers crash.

Zero Taxpayer Cost: Built independently without a single dollar of public funding, proving how open data can replace clunky bureaucracy with clean, accessible design.

Permanent Public Archive: Unlike official maps that suffer from "digital decay" after decennial redistricting, the platform preserves past district lines, ballots, and candidate links year-over-year.

Open-Source Offer: After catching the attention of state officials, including Senator Mike Shower and the Lieutenant Governor, Izon has offered to open-source the codebase and hand the entire tool over to the state at no cost.

When civic-minded developers pair open data with good design, they can build the reliable public infrastructure citizens actually deserve.

text:
25 years ago, I co-wrote this article with Lee Kaplan. Reviewing it today, I see what has changed, & what feels sadly familiar about the conflict between Israel and Hamas in Gaza today.  -- BJ 

"Most Asked Questions about the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict"

By Becky Johnson & Lee Kaplan
   August 12, 2002
 Published by:   https://t.co/OfrpmsKaAN

-- Didn't Israel drive out 600,000 Palestinians at gunpoint in 1948 and take their land?

Most Arabs who left Israel did so under the orders of the Arab leader, the Grand Mufti, to withdraw and let the Arab armies "drive the Jews into the sea," which they attempted in 1948. However Israel won that war. Not all of the Arabs left, and Israel is now 18% Arab. These Arabs have full citizenship rights, can own property, vote, and have 14 representatives in the Knesset, the Israeli Parliament.

-- I've heard that some Israelis say there is no such thing as Palestinians. How can they say that?

Up until the 1967 war, the Arabs living in Israel did not even call themselves Palestinians -- twenty years after the founding of the modern state of Israel. The name Palestine came from the Romans who destroyed the Jewish Temple in Jerusalem in 70 AD. To humiliate the Jews, the Romans renamed the land Palestine after their mortal enemies, the Philistines. The modern land of Palestine was given that name by the British when they took control over from the crumbling Ottoman Empire. In British Palestine, both Jews and Arabs were Palestinians.

(See "What is a Palestinian?" at Masada 2000)

-- Why doesn't Israel just give back the West Bank to the Palestinians? Then there will be peace.

In 1948, Israel's Arab neighbors tried to destroy the State of Israel. They rejected a Palestinian State, which the UN offered them at the same time as when Israel was founded. Prior to 1967, the West Bank was part of Jordan. Currently Jordan has a peace treaty with Israel. The West Bank, which Jews call Judea and Samaria, is part of the ancient kingdom of Israel, and has been home to Arabs and Jews for thousands of years. Arafat himself said he will take back Israel in its entirety, if he has to do it all at once or piece by piece.

--  Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon is looking for any excuse to invade and shoot Palestinians. Why did the Israeli people even elect him?

The directives given the IDF are strictly against the taking of innocent civilian life. Sharon withdrew ELEVEN times from the West Bank to effect a cease-fire. Each time Israel was attacked by suicide bombers. The Palestinian Authority failed to arrest them And instead paid their families awards. They even named streets after them as "martyrs". How can anyone take an enemy seriously that encourages the terror attacks? In 2000, President Clinton and Prime Minister Barak tried to offer the Palestinians a state, which included 95% of the West Bank. Arafat rejected the offer and launched the latest intifada or uprising. The sniper killings and suicide bombings are the method used to attack Israeli citizens. The Israeli people, who were angered when Arafat rejected Barak's offer, elected the hard-liner Sharon by a landslide. Sharon has prevented more terror attacks than he has instigated. To blame him for the terror attacks is like blaming a woman for being raped.

 -- Why are there so many more dead Palestinians than dead Israelis? Doesn't this prove that Israel is the aggressor here?

Several reasons combine to explain the differential death toll. First, the numbers are skewed. The Palestinians count the suicide bombers as "civilian casualties". They also count terrorists killed in shootouts with the police or IDF. Fact is, if civilians were only counted, Israeli casualties would be higher. Snipers who open fire on civilians are immediately hunted down and arrested, but many fight until they are shot. A big factor appears to be Palestinian gunmen who hide themselves in populated areas, which causes a high civilian death toll when the IDF tries to shoot back at them. The IDF has a policy of a measured response to a terrorist attack. These reprisals rarely involve death or injury. Also, given the P.A.'s problems with math, such as claiming 1,500 killed in Jenin when it was 52, their calculations are highly suspect. Israel has 10,000 people who are invalids, in comas or scarred in other ways for life.

 -- Wait a minute! Israel has a heavily armed state-of-the-art military and the Palestinians only have rocks and a few old guns. Shouldn't our sympathies be with the Palestinians who only want their freedom from oppression and the opportunity for self-rule?

The Palestinians are using more than rocks, although stonings can be very violent too, causing death and serious injury. They have Qasem rockets. They have grenades. They have M-16's and Kalashnikovs [Ed.: Russian made assault rifles]. Arafat demanded weapons claiming he needed an armed police force to keep order. Those guns, provided by none other than Israel, have been linked with numerous terrorist attacks. Many weapons have been smuggled in from Egypt as well. The Palestinian police ARE the terrorists such as Fatah and Al Aksa. Currently the Palestinians, have self-rule under the Oslo accords yet persist in attacking Israel.

 -- Don't the Israelis build roads and freeways that bypass Palestinian villages and they aren't allowed to use them?

They do bypass them. They were built because when Israelis drive by them they are shot at or have rocks thrown at them. Boulders dropped from heights above the roads have killed some. If the Israelis built freeways on Arab land, they'd complain the Israelis were taking Arab land or that they were damaging the environment.

 -- Every time a Palestinian wants to go somewhere they have to go thru an Israeli checkpoint. Isn't this humiliating for the Palestinian people?

Humiliating? US citizens have to wait two hours at checkpoints at the airport. It's called security against terrorism. Suicide bombers kill Arabs too.

 -- The Israeli Defense Force (IDF) regularly prevents ambulances from picking up sick and wounded people. Isn't this a crime against humanity?

They don't prevent medical care. However, time and time again the Arabs have transported bombs and terrorists in ambulances so now they must be thoroughly checked. Israel gives free medical care to many Palestinians. In Jenin last April, the IDF supplied blood to the hospital for wounded Palestinians. But the blood was rejected because the Palestinians would not use Jewish blood. So the IDF using military transports brought in blood from Jordan.

 --  -- The Israelis have stopped the Palestinians from normal commerce, from employment, and now they are suffering from food shortages. How can they justify this?

Commerce and employment were higher when Israel controlled the area. In nine years with billions of dollars in aid the PA has failed even to feed its people. PA warlords under Arafat control UN food allotments and even sell it on the black market. It has been the terrorist attacks that have made business as usual impossible and have hurt the Palestinian economy.

 -- When the Israelis say that the Arabs only wish to drive them into the sea, aren't they just being paranoid and using this as an excuse to justify their aggression against the Palestinians?

5.5 million Jews. 250 million Arabs. Missiles with germ and radioactivel warheads on Israel's northern frontier controlled by Hezbollah. 21 terrorist attacks a day against common Israelis. The Arabs said "into the sea" in 1948 and even after Oslo. This is paranoid???

 -- Didn't the International Conference in Durban, South Africa condemn Israel as a racist state?

The conference was made up of Arab dictatorships pushing their own agenda. The US and most of Europe boycotted the vote.

 -- The Palestinians and the Jews have been fighting for thousands of years. Aren't they equally responsible for the violence?

They have not been fighting for thousands of years. The Arabs persecuted Jews. The difference is the Arabs won't tolerate a Jewish presence in the Muslim Middle East -- period. The Jews offer to negotiate peace but the Arabs are really just negotiating the end of Israel.

 -- The suicide bombings are terrible, but aren't they done by a small handful of extremists? Isn't it wrong to condemn all the Palestinian people for the acts of a few?

Evidence shows that as many as twelve extremist groups conduct terrorist attacks against Israeli citizens. Hamas, Hezbollah, The Al Aqsa Martyrs Brigade, and Fatah are a few of them.
